Theatrical lighting and dramatic chiaroscuro
Preserved at the Alte Pinakothek in Munich
Commissioned by Prince Frederick Henry of Orange-Nassau

slaughtered-ox.title: The Slaughtered Ox
slaughtered-ox.description: A brutal still life that would influence Soutine and Bacon.
descriptions: Painted by Rembrandt in 1655
Oil on wood measuring 94 x 67 cm
Brutal still life that shocked the 17th century
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Inspired Soutine, Bacon and many other modernists

philosopher-meditation.title: Philosopher in Meditation
philosopher-meditation.description: A mysterious interior with a spiral staircase.
descriptions: Painted by Rembrandt in 1632
Oil on wood measuring 28 x 34 cm
Spiral staircase became an emblematic motif of the painter
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Subject often identified as Tobit at the start of the night

danae-rembrandt.title: Danaë
danae-rembrandt.description: A mythological nude with masterful chiaroscuro.
descriptions: Painted by Rembrandt between 1636 and 1647
Oil on canvas measuring 1.85 x 2.03 meters
Vandalized with acid in 1985, restored over 12 years
Preserved at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
Face inspired successively by his wife Saskia, then Geertje

elevation-cross.title: The Elevation of the Cross
elevation-cross.description: A monumental triptych showing the moment the cross is raised.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens between 1610 and 1611
Oil on wood, triptych for Antwerp Cathedral
Twin triptych to the Descent from the Cross
Visible at the Cathedral of Our Lady in Antwerp
Rubens's first major commission upon his return from Italy

judgment-paris-rubens.title: The Judgment of Paris
judgment-paris-rubens.description: The three goddesses appear nude before the Trojan prince.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens around 1632-1635
Oil on wood measuring 1.45 x 1.94 meters
The three goddesses present themselves naked before the Trojan prince
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
The subject allowed Rubens to display his female nudes

samson-delilah.title: Samson and Delilah
samson-delilah.description: Delilah betrays the sleeping Samson by cutting his hair.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens around 1609-1610
Oil on wood measuring 1.85 x 2.05 meters
Delilah betrays sleeping Samson by cutting his hair
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
Attribution recently debated by experts

massacre-innocents-rubens.title: The Massacre of the Innocents
massacre-innocents-rubens.description: Soldiers tearing children from their mothers, a scene of ancient carnage.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens around 1611
Oil on wood measuring 1.42 x 1.82 meters
Sold for 76 million dollars at Sotheby's in 2002
Preserved at the Art Gallery of Ontario in Toronto
Discovered in 2001 in a basement after misattribution

marie-medici-cycle.title: The Marie de' Medici Cycle
marie-medici-cycle.description: 24 monumental paintings celebrating the life of the queen of France.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens between 1622 and 1625
Cycle of 24 monumental canvases for the Luxembourg Palace
Idealized and allegorical life of Queen Marie de' Medici
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris in the Medici Gallery
Marie de' Medici never paid the full commission to Rubens

susanna-elders-rubens.title: Susanna and the Elders
susanna-elders-rubens.description: The chaste Susanna surprised at her bath by two lecherous old men.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens around 1606-1607
Oil on canvas during his Italian stay in Rome
Susanna surprised at her bath by two lecherous elders
Preserved at the Borghese Gallery in Rome
Rubens revisited this biblical subject in several versions

chateau-steen.title: Het Steen
chateau-steen.description: A panoramic landscape of Rubens's country estate.
descriptions: Painted by Rubens around 1636
Oil on wood measuring 1.31 x 2.29 meters
Depicts the estate acquired by Rubens in 1635
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
Rubens spent the last years of his life there

charles-i-horse.title: Charles I on Horseback
charles-i-horse.description: An equestrian portrait of the King of England.
descriptions: Painted by Van Dyck around 1637-1638
Oil on canvas measuring 3.67 x 2.92 meters
Official royal image visible in the Whitehall galleries
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
Van Dyck would die in 1641, shortly before the king beheaded in 1649

charles-i-hunting.title: Charles I at the Hunt
charles-i-hunting.description: The king in casual attire in an English landscape.
descriptions: Painted by Van Dyck around 1635
Oil on canvas measuring 2.66 x 2.07 meters
The king in civilian dress before his horse, elegant pose
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Louis XIV personally acquired it in 1738

self-portrait-sunflower.title: Self-Portrait with a Sunflower
self-portrait-sunflower.description: Van Dyck depicts himself pointing to a sunflower, symbol of loyalty.
descriptions: Painted by Van Dyck around 1633
Oil on canvas depicting the painter near a sunflower
Sunflower symbolizes loyalty to Charles I
Preserved in a private collection
Van Dyck proudly wore the gold chain given by the king

triple-portrait-charles.title: Triple Portrait of Charles I
triple-portrait-charles.description: Three views of the king to serve as a model for a bust.
descriptions: Painted by Van Dyck in 1635-1636
Oil on canvas depicting three views of the king
Designed to serve as a model for a Bernini bust in Rome
Preserved in the Royal Collection in London
The sculpted bust was destroyed in the 1698 Whitehall fire

portrait-henrietta-maria.title: Portrait of Henrietta Maria
portrait-henrietta-maria.description: The Queen of England in ceremonial dress.
descriptions: Painted by Van Dyck around 1632
Oil on canvas depicting the Queen of England
Henrietta Maria was the daughter of Henry IV of France
Preserved in the Royal Collection in London
Van Dyck painted more than 25 different portraits of the queen

laughing-cavalier.title: The Laughing Cavalier
laughing-cavalier.description: Joyful portrait of an elegant young man with a mischievous smile.
descriptions: Painted by Frans Hals in 1624
Oil on canvas measuring 83 x 67 cm
The subject is neither a cavalier nor fully laughing, but smiling
Preserved at the Wallace Collection in London
Nickname popularized by art dealers in the 19th century

malle-babbe.title: Malle Babbe
malle-babbe.description: A striking portrait of a woman at the tavern with her owl.
descriptions: Painted by Frans Hals around 1633-1635
Oil on canvas measuring 75 x 64 cm
Depicts a famous alcoholic woman of Haarlem
Preserved at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin
The owl on her shoulder symbolizes madness or drunkenness

regents-haarlem.title: The Regentesses of the Old Men's Almshouse
regents-haarlem.description: A late group portrait in dark and severe tones.
descriptions: Painted by Frans Hals in 1664
Oil on canvas measuring 1.7 x 2.5 meters
Frans Hals himself was a resident of the almshouse at age 80
Preserved at the Frans Hals Museum in Haarlem
One of his most merciless late works

gypsy-girl-hals.title: The Gypsy Girl
gypsy-girl-hals.description: The mischievous smile of a young woman of the people.
descriptions: Painted by Frans Hals around 1628-1630
Oil on wood measuring 58 x 52 cm
Spontaneous smile rare in 17th-century portraiture
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Model unknown, but probably a young woman of the people

courtyard-delft.title: Courtyard of a House in Delft
courtyard-delft.description: A peaceful domestic scene with architectural play of light.
descriptions: Painted by Pieter de Hooch in 1658
Oil on canvas measuring 73.5 x 60 cm
Tiles and architecture rendered with photographic precision
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
De Hooch was a contemporary of Vermeer in Delft

mother-lacing-bodice.title: Woman Lacing Her Bodice
mother-lacing-bodice.description: Domestic intimacy and characteristic Dutch light.
descriptions: Painted by Pieter de Hooch around 1659-1660
Oil on canvas typical of Dutch genre painting
Warm light streaming through a window, a recurring motif
Preserved at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin
Cradle and dog complete the peaceful domestic scene

woman-child-pantry.title: Woman and Child in a Pantry
woman-child-pantry.description: Intimate scene with a perspective toward the outside, typical play of light.
descriptions: Painted by Pieter de Hooch around 1656-1660
Oil on canvas depicting a domestic scene
Perspective opening outdoors, bold depth effect
Preserved at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam
Woman serving a drink to a child in a pantry

goldfinch.title: The Goldfinch
goldfinch.description: A small chained bird, a work made famous by Donna Tartt's novel.
descriptions: Painted by Carel Fabritius in 1654
Oil on wood measuring 33.5 x 22.8 cm
Painted the year of Fabritius's death in the Delft explosion
Preserved at the Mauritshuis in The Hague
Direct inspiration for Donna Tartt's famous 2013 novel

sentry-fabritius.title: The Sentry
sentry-fabritius.description: A soldier dozing before a doorway, with bold perspective.
descriptions: Painted by Carel Fabritius in 1654
Oil on canvas depicting a dozing soldier
Bold perspective worthy of his master Rembrandt
Preserved at the Staatliches Museum in Schwerin
One of his last works before his tragic death

view-delft-fabritius.title: View of Delft
view-delft-fabritius.description: A wide-angle view of the city with a church and a musical instrument.
descriptions: Painted by Carel Fabritius in 1652
Oil on canvas measuring 15.4 x 31.6 cm, panoramic format
Possibly designed for a perspective box
Preserved at the National Gallery in London
Fabritius died in 1654 in the Delft powder magazine explosion

cheat-ace-diamonds.title: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
cheat-ace-diamonds.description: Scene of cheating at cards, with complicit glances and a naive victim.
descriptions: Painted by Georges de La Tour around 1635
Oil on canvas measuring 1.06 x 1.46 meters
Three cheats rob a naive young man
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The Louvre's 1972 purchase considered the acquisition of the century

magdalene-candle.title: Magdalene with the Smoking Flame
magdalene-candle.description: A meditative figure lit by a candle, chiaroscuro of great intimacy.
descriptions: Painted by Georges de La Tour around 1640
Oil on canvas depicting Mary Magdalene in meditation
Candlelit chiaroscuro, La Tour's stylistic signature
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
La Tour was rediscovered in the 20th century after being forgotten

newborn-la-tour.title: The Newborn
newborn-la-tour.description: Two women contemplating a newborn by candlelight.
descriptions: Painted by Georges de La Tour around 1645-1648
Oil on canvas measuring 76 x 91 cm
Two women contemplating a baby illuminated by a candle
Preserved at the Musée des Beaux-Arts in Rennes
One of the painter's tenderest and most silent works

st-joseph-carpenter.title: Saint Joseph the Carpenter
st-joseph-carpenter.description: The child Jesus illuminates Joseph's work by candlelight.
descriptions: Painted by Georges de La Tour around 1642
Oil on canvas measuring 1.37 x 1.02 meters
The child Jesus illuminates Joseph's face with a candle
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Donated by Percy Moore Turner to the Louvre in 1948

the-ray.title: The Ray
the-ray.description: A striking still life with a skinned ray, cat, and kitchen utensils.
descriptions: Painted by Chardin in 1728
Oil on canvas measuring 1.14 x 1.46 meters
Reception piece for the Royal Academy of Painting
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Diderot saw in the skinned ray the true nature of flesh

grace-chardin.title: Grace before the Meal
grace-chardin.description: Mother and children reciting prayer before the meal, a sober domestic scene.
descriptions: Painted by Chardin around 1740
Oil on canvas measuring 49 x 38 cm
Mother and children reciting prayer before the meal
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Acquired by Louis XV for the Royal Collection in 1740

house-cards-chardin.title: The House of Cards
house-cards-chardin.description: A young man absorbed in building a fragile house of cards.
descriptions: Painted by Chardin around 1737
Oil on canvas depicting a child absorbed in his game
Variation on the theme of vanity and fragility
Preserved at the National Gallery of Art in Washington
Chardin revisited this subject in several versions

soap-bubbles-chardin.title: Soap Bubbles
soap-bubbles-chardin.description: A young man blowing a bubble, a vanitas on the fragility of life.
descriptions: Painted by Chardin around 1733-1734
Oil on canvas measuring 93 x 74.6 cm
Modern vanitas: the bubble evokes the brevity of life
Preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
The young man and his little brother probably the painter's sons

embarkation-cythera.title: The Embarkation for Cythera
embarkation-cythera.description: Mythical fête galante in which couples leave the island of love in a dreamy landscape.
descriptions: Painted by Watteau in 1717
Oil on canvas measuring 1.29 x 1.94 meters
Watteau's admission piece for the Royal Academy
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
A second version exists at the Charlottenburg Palace in Berlin

pierrot-gilles.title: Pierrot (Gilles)
pierrot-gilles.description: The commedia dell'arte character alone facing the viewer, melancholy and isolated.
descriptions: Painted by Watteau around 1718-1719
Oil on canvas measuring 1.84 x 1.49 meters
Pierrot alone facing the viewer, unusual melancholic attitude
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Acquired for the Louvre in 1869 by Louis La Caze

shop-sign-gersaint.title: L'Enseigne de Gersaint
shop-sign-gersaint.description: Watteau's last work, a scene of an art gallery — his artistic testament.
descriptions: Painted by Watteau in 1720
Oil on canvas measuring 1.66 x 3.06 meters
Watteau's last work, painted in eight days at age 36
Preserved at the Charlottenburg Palace in Berlin
Served as a shop sign for art dealer Gersaint in Paris

fetes-venitiennes.title: Fêtes Vénitiennes
fetes-venitiennes.description: Couples dancing in a park, elegance and poetry of the fête galante.
descriptions: Painted by Watteau around 1718-1719
Oil on canvas measuring 56 x 46 cm
Watteau himself plays bagpipes on the right of the painting
Preserved at the Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh
One of his last fêtes galantes before his death in 1721

the-swing.title: The Swing
the-swing.description: Icon of Rococo, a young woman on a swing in a lush garden.
descriptions: Painted by Fragonard in 1767
Oil on canvas measuring 81 x 64 cm
Commissioned by the Baron de Saint-Julien for his mistress
Preserved at the Wallace Collection in London
Absolute icon of French Rococo and libertine gallantry

the-bolt.title: The Bolt
the-bolt.description: A scene of passionate seduction, the man closing the bedroom bolt.
descriptions: Painted by Fragonard around 1776-1779
Oil on canvas measuring 73 x 93 cm
Passionate seduction scene, the man locks the door
Preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Possible counterpart to the Adoration of the Shepherds, painted in series

reader-fragonard.title: A Young Girl Reading
reader-fragonard.description: A young woman absorbed in her reading, with delicate profile and lemon-yellow dress.
descriptions: Painted by Fragonard around 1770-1772
Oil on canvas measuring 81 x 65 cm
Delicate profile of a young woman in a lemon-yellow dress
Preserved at the National Gallery of Art in Washington
Donated by Andrew Mellon to the NGA in 1961

stolen-kiss.title: The Stolen Kiss
stolen-kiss.description: A stolen kiss in an antechamber — an intimate late-18th-century scene.
descriptions: Painted by Fragonard around 1786-1788
Oil on canvas measuring 45 x 55 cm
Seduction scene in an antechamber, elegant intimacy
Preserved at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
One of Fragonard's last major works

impression-sunrise.title: Impression, Sunrise
impression-sunrise.description: This painting gave its name to the Impressionist movement at its first exhibition in 1874.
descriptions: Painted in 1872 from a hotel room overlooking the port of Le Havre at dawn
Monet used only a few quick brushstrokes of pure colors
Critic Louis Leroy mocked the title, unintentionally coining the word 'Impressionism'
Preserved at the Musée Marmottan Monet in Paris since 1940
Stolen in 1985 and recovered five years later in Corsica

water-lilies-1906.title: Water Lilies
water-lilies-1906.description: Monet painted about 250 canvases of his water garden at Giverny over 30 years.
descriptions: Monet painted about 250 water lily canvases over thirty years at Giverny
He had a pond dug and planted exotic water lilies
This 1906 version shows only the water surface, with no bank or sky
Displayed at the Art Institute of Chicago in its Impressionist gallery
Late in life, Monet suffered from cataracts which influenced his colors

japanese-bridge.title: The Water Lily Pond
japanese-bridge.description: The Japanese bridge in Monet's garden became one of his most iconic subjects.
descriptions: Monet had this green bridge built in his Giverny garden in 1893
He drew inspiration from the Japanese prints he collected
He painted the bridge more than 18 times under different lights
The purple wisteria covering it were planted later
The garden at Giverny now attracts over 500,000 visitors per year

rouen-cathedral.title: Rouen Cathedral
rouen-cathedral.description: Monet painted more than 30 views of the cathedral at different hours and seasons.
descriptions: Monet painted more than 30 views of the cathedral between 1892 and 1894
He rented a room facing the monument to track the light
He worked on several canvases simultaneously depending on the hour
The Gothic cathedral of Rouen is one of the tallest in France
Cézanne hailed this series as a pictorial revolution

woman-parasol.title: Woman with a Parasol
woman-parasol.description: Portrait of Camille, Monet's wife, and their son Jean in summer light.
descriptions: Painted in 1875, this painting shows Camille Monet and her son Jean aged seven
Monet captured the scene in a few hours to catch the wind
The sky is visible through the transparent veil of the white dress
The green shadow on Camille's face was bold for the time
Camille would die four years later at just 32

gare-saint-lazare.title: The Gare Saint-Lazare
gare-saint-lazare.description: The modernity of the steam locomotive captured in Impressionist swirls of smoke.
descriptions: Monet painted twelve views of the Saint-Lazare station in 1877
He obtained special permission from the company to set up on the platforms
Steam locomotives were a symbol of industrial modernity
Émile Zola would draw inspiration from this station for his novel The Human Beast
This canvas is displayed at the Musée d'Orsay, itself a former train station

moulin-galette.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
moulin-galette.description: A scene of a popular Parisian festival, a masterpiece of Impressionist joie de vivre.
descriptions: Renoir painted this scene in 1876 in a popular Montmartre dance hall
He depicted his painter friends and neighborhood models there
The patches of light through the trees revolutionized open-air painting
The canvas measures almost two meters long
A second version sold for 78 million dollars in 1990

luncheon-boating.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
luncheon-boating.description: Renoir depicted his future wife Aline and several of his friends here.
descriptions: Painted in 1881 at the Maison Fournaise on the Seine near Chatou
Shows Aline Charigot, Renoir's future wife, playing with a small dog
The painting brings together fourteen figures, almost all friends of the painter
Caillebotte appears seated on the right wearing a white boater hat
Acquired in 1923 by collector Duncan Phillips in Washington

dance-bougival.title: Dance at Bougival
dance-bougival.description: A celebration of the popular joy of the dance halls along the Seine.
descriptions: Renoir painted this canvas in 1883 at the Bougival guinguette
The female model is Suzanne Valadon, a future famous painter
The man in the yellow hat is Paul Lhote, Renoir's friend
The painting is part of a series of three dances commissioned by Durand-Ruel
It has been displayed at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston since 1937

grandes-baigneuses.title: The Large Bathers
grandes-baigneuses.description: Renoir moves away from Impressionism here toward a more classical style.
descriptions: Renoir worked on this painting for three years between 1884 and 1887
He drew inspiration from Girardon's nymph bas-relief at Versailles
The sharp outlines mark a break from his Impressionist style
Aline Charigot posed for the main figure in the foreground
The Philadelphia Museum of Art acquired it in 1963 through a bequest

dance-class.title: The Dance Class
dance-class.description: Degas devoted much of his work to the dancers of the Paris Opera.
descriptions: Degas painted this scene around 1874 in the rehearsal room of the Opéra
The ballet master depicted is Jules Perrot, a famous choreographer
Degas didn't like being called an Impressionist; he preferred 'realist'
He produced over 1,500 works on the theme of dancers
The painting is one of the most visited works at the Musée d'Orsay

absinthe.title: L'Absinthe
absinthe.description: A portrait of urban loneliness, showing actress Ellen Andrée and printmaker Marcellin Desboutin.
descriptions: Painted in 1876, the work shows a café on the Place Pigalle
The models are actress Ellen Andrée and artist Marcellin Desboutin
The painting caused scandal for its social criticism in England
Absinthe would be banned in France in 1915 for its supposed effects
Degas uses an unusual perspective with an empty table in the foreground

little-dancer.title: Little Dancer of Fourteen Years
little-dancer.description: Revolutionary sculpture with real hair and a fabric tutu.
descriptions: Wax sculpture presented in 1881 at an Impressionist exhibition
The model is Marie van Goethem, a young student at the Paris Opera
The addition of real hair, tutu and slippers caused scandal
Twenty-eight posthumous bronzes were cast after Degas's death
A version sold for 24.9 million dollars in 2022

ballet-rehearsal.title: Ballet Rehearsal on Stage
ballet-rehearsal.description: Innovative overhead view of the wings of the Opera.
descriptions: Painted around 1874, this pastel innovates through its asymmetric composition
Degas drew inspiration from photographic and Japanese framing
The dancers are seen from the conductor's box
On the right, two subscribers in black coats can be seen observing the young girls
The dry pastel allowed Degas to layer colors

olympia.title: Olympia
olympia.description: This provocative nude of a Parisian courtesan caused a scandal at the Salon of 1865.
descriptions: Manet painted Olympia in 1863 but exhibited it only in 1865
The model is Victorine Meurent, a painter herself
The painting caused scandal and had to be protected by two guards
Manet drew inspiration from Titian's Venus of Urbino
The black ribbon and slipper unambiguously evoked prostitution

dejeuner-herbe.title: Luncheon on the Grass
dejeuner-herbe.description: A nude woman picnicking with clothed men shocked the public at the Salon des Refusés.
descriptions: Manet painted this work in 1863 after a drawing by Raphael
Rejected by the official Salon, it was exhibited at the Salon des Refusés
Napoleon III reportedly called the painting immodest
The original title was simply The Bath
The work is considered the founding act of modern painting

bar-folies-bergere.title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
bar-folies-bergere.description: Manet's last great work, playing with the reflections of the mirror.
descriptions: Manet painted it in 1882, a year before his death
The model is Suzon, a real waitress at the Folies Bergère
The mirror behind her poses an enigma about the offset reflection
The bottles show champagne, beer and grenadine
The work has been preserved at the Courtauld Gallery in London since 1932

fifer.title: The Fifer
fifer.description: Bold portrait of a young military musician against a neutral background.
descriptions: Manet painted The Fifer in 1866 after a trip to Spain
He drew inspiration from Velázquez and Japanese prints
The painting was rejected by the 1866 Salon
The model is a young military musician from the Imperial Guard
Émile Zola strongly defended the painting in the press

cradle.title: The Cradle
cradle.description: One of the founders of Impressionism, depicting her sister watching over her child.
descriptions: Berthe Morisot painted her sister Edma watching over her niece in 1872
It is the first work shown at the first Impressionist exhibition of 1874
Morisot was the only woman to exhibit at this historic event
The muslin veil creates a remarkable transparency effect
Acquired by the Musée d'Orsay in 1930, it is one of the museum's flagships

reading.title: Reading
reading.description: An intimate scene of bourgeois female life.
descriptions: Painted in 1873, this work shows the artist's sister, Edma
Morisot favored intimate female scenes from her circle
She used a light palette with lots of whites
The Cleveland Museum of Art has preserved this work since 1950
Morisot was the sister-in-law of Édouard Manet, with whom she often associated

summer-day-morisot.title: Summer's Day
summer-day-morisot.description: Two women in a boat on the lake of the Bois de Boulogne.
descriptions: Painted in 1879, this work captures a boat ride
Morisot created the work directly on the spot at the Bois de Boulogne
The quick brushstrokes evoke reflections on the water
The National Gallery in London acquired it in 1917
Morisot was a pioneer in observing urban leisure

eugene-manet-morisot.title: Eugène Manet on the Isle of Wight
eugene-manet-morisot.description: Portrait of her husband looking out the window, in summer light.
descriptions: Painted in 1875 during the couple's honeymoon
Eugène Manet, Berthe's husband, is the brother of painter Édouard Manet
Sailboats can be seen through the window in the port of Cowes
The canvas combines intimate interior and maritime landscape
It is preserved at the Musée Marmottan Monet in Paris

pont-neuf.title: Pont Neuf
pont-neuf.description: Lively view of Paris's oldest bridge bathed in light.
descriptions: Renoir painted the Pont-Neuf in 1872 from a window above
His brother Edmond helped stop passersby to talk to them
Renoir thus had more time to sketch them in motion
The Pont-Neuf is the oldest bridge in Paris, completed in 1607
The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds this work

poppy-field.title: Poppies
poppy-field.description: Camille and Jean Monet walking through a field of flowers near Argenteuil.
descriptions: Painted in 1873 in Argenteuil where Monet was then living
Camille Monet and their son Jean appear twice in the painting
The poppies form bright red patches against the green grass
The work was shown at the first Impressionist exhibition of 1874
The Musée d'Orsay displays it in its Monet room

paris-rainy-day.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
paris-rainy-day.description: Bold perspective of a Parisian intersection in the rain.
descriptions: Caillebotte painted this scene in 1877 on the Place de Dublin
The canvas measures over two meters wide
Caillebotte depicts the new boulevards created by Haussmann
The bold perspective recalls photographic views
The Art Institute of Chicago acquired it in 1964 for 75,000 dollars

haystacks-end-summer.title: Haystacks, End of Summer
haystacks-end-summer.description: Series of 25 canvases showing haystacks at different hours.
descriptions: This canvas is part of the 25-haystack series painted in 1890-1891
Monet painted the haystacks in a field neighboring his Giverny house
He studied light variations by hour and season
The series sold out in a few days at the 1891 exhibition
One version reached 110.7 million dollars in 2019 at Sotheby's

haystacks-sunset.title: Haystacks at Sunset
haystacks-sunset.description: Evening light effects on the haystacks.
descriptions: Painted around 1891, this version captures the reds of twilight
Monet worked simultaneously on several canvases depending on the hour
The peasant Cécile brought him canvases as the light changed
The haystacks were up to six meters tall at the time
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston owns several versions of the series

rouen-cathedral-morning.title: Rouen Cathedral, the Morning
rouen-cathedral-morning.description: The Gothic facade bathed in morning light.
descriptions: Painted between 1892 and 1894, this version captures dawn on the stone
Monet used up to fourteen different canvases per day
He applied paint in thick layers to evoke the stone
Twenty canvases of the series were exhibited at Durand-Ruel in 1895
Pissarro wrote that it was a revelation for modern painters

rouen-cathedral-sunset.title: Rouen Cathedral at Sunset
rouen-cathedral-sunset.description: The cathedral in the golden light of evening.
descriptions: This canvas captures the orange tones of the setting sun
Monet paid 75 francs per month to rent three rooms facing the cathedral
He called his work a 'nightmare' because of the difficulty
The French State refused to buy the complete series in 1895
The Marmottan Museum preserves this golden version

parliament-fog.title: Houses of Parliament in the Fog
parliament-fog.description: The Thames shrouded in mist with Parliament in the background.
descriptions: Monet made several trips to London between 1899 and 1901
He stayed at the Savoy Hotel with a view of the Thames
He then finished the canvases in Giverny from memory and photos
The London fog fascinated Monet with its colored effects
The Art Institute of Chicago displays this misty version

water-lilies-green.title: Green Water Lilies
water-lilies-green.description: Water lily pond with dominant green reflections.
descriptions: This version shows almost exclusively the aquatic vegetation
Monet called his garden his 'greatest masterpiece'
He employed seven gardeners to maintain the pond
Green reflections dominate the composition without a horizon line
The Musée d'Orsay preserves several versions of the Water Lilies

japanese-bridge-1900.title: The Water Lily Pond, Green Harmony
japanese-bridge-1900.description: The Japanese bridge in its green surroundings.
descriptions: Painted around 1899, this canvas shows the bridge without wisteria
Monet planted his water garden in 1893 on a piece of land he bought
He had a branch of the Epte river diverted to feed the pond
The fluid style heralds the great decorative panels of the Orangerie
Several versions of the bridge are displayed at the Musée d'Orsay

regatta-argenteuil.title: Regattas at Argenteuil
regatta-argenteuil.description: Sailboats on the Seine, with colored reflections in the water.
descriptions: Painted in 1872, this canvas shows the Seine at Argenteuil
Monet lived in Argenteuil where he had set up his floating studio
Manet, Renoir and Sisley came to paint with him on site
The white-hulled sailboats reflect in the blue water
The canvas is displayed in the Monet gallery at the Musée d'Orsay

woman-garden.title: Woman in a Garden
woman-garden.description: Female figure in a flowery garden.
descriptions: This canvas is part of a series of figures in gardens
Monet favored female models from his circle
The flowers create a chromatic explosion typical of Monet
The Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg preserves this work
Catherine the Great had initiated the museum's French collection

la-grenouillere.title: La Grenouillère
la-grenouillere.description: Dance hall on the Seine where Monet and Renoir painted together.
descriptions: La Grenouillère was a floating café-restaurant on the Seine at Croissy
Monet and Renoir painted there side by side in 1869
Napoleon III came to bathe there with his court
This canvas foreshadows the divided brushstroke of Impressionism
The Metropolitan Museum in New York acquired it in 1929

garden-sainte-adresse.title: Garden at Sainte-Adresse
garden-sainte-adresse.description: Flower terrace overlooking the sea with flags.
descriptions: Painted in 1867 on the family estate near Le Havre
Monet's father can be seen sitting with a hat
The French and Japanese flags fly in the breeze
The flat perspective is inspired by Japanese prints
The Met acquired it in 1967 for 1.4 million dollars, a museum record

dejeuner-monet.title: The Luncheon
dejeuner-monet.description: An intimate family scene around the table.
descriptions: Painted around 1868, this work shows the Monet family at Étretat
Young Jean Monet is seated at the table with his mother
The painting was rejected by the 1870 Salon
Monet sent it to the 1874 Impressionist exhibition
It is preserved at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt, Germany

capucines-boulevard.title: Boulevard des Capucines
capucines-boulevard.description: Lively view of a Parisian boulevard in winter.
descriptions: Painted in 1873 from the studio of photographer Nadar
The work was exhibited at the first Impressionist exhibition of 1874
Critic Leroy mocked the 'blackish' silhouettes of the passersby
This high-angle view is very modern for the time
The Pushkin Museum in Moscow preserves this version

venice-twilight.title: The Grand Canal, Venice
venice-twilight.description: Venice in the light of twilight.
descriptions: Monet stayed in Venice for two months in 1908
He painted 37 views of the city in only 70 days
The work captures the evening light on the water
His wife Alice accompanied him on this trip
The series was exhibited at Bernheim-Jeune in Paris in 1912

swing-renoir.title: The Swing
swing-renoir.description: Young woman on a swing, with light filtering through the foliage.
descriptions: Painted in 1876, the same year as the Bal du moulin de la Galette
The model is Jeanne, a young woman from the Montmartre neighborhood
Renoir uses the technique of patches of light through leaves
The blue rounds on the dress create an Impressionist effect
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved the work since 1894

girls-piano.title: Girls at the Piano
girls-piano.description: Two sisters learning the piano, the first work acquired by the State.
descriptions: Renoir painted five versions of this scene in 1892
The French State bought one of them for the Musée du Luxembourg
It was the first Renoir work bought by the State
Renoir wanted to depict bourgeois musical education
The harmonies of blues and pinks are characteristic of his late period

moulin-huet-bay.title: Moulin Huet Bay
moulin-huet-bay.description: Seascape of Guernsey with brilliant colors.
descriptions: Renoir stayed in Guernsey for a month in 1883
He painted fifteen canvases there inspired by the island's light
The bay has remained almost unchanged since Renoir's time
The work is preserved at the National Gallery in London
Victor Hugo had also stayed in Guernsey in exile

bathers-renoir.title: The Bathers
bathers-renoir.description: Renoir's last great work, his artistic testament.
descriptions: Renoir painted this last great canvas in 1918-1919
Suffering from arthritis, he painted with brushes attached to his hand
The models are his servant Andrée Heuschling and Catherine Hessling
The painting was given to the Louvre by Renoir's sons
It is now displayed at the Musée d'Orsay

umbrellas.title: The Umbrellas
umbrellas.description: Parisian street scene in the rain.
descriptions: Renoir painted this scene between 1881 and 1886, in two stages
The figures on the right show his early Impressionist style
The figures on the left reveal his return to a sharper drawing
A young girl with a hoop appears in the foreground
The National Gallery in London has preserved this work since 1917

la-loge.title: La Loge
la-loge.description: Elegant couple in a theater box.
descriptions: Painted in 1874 for the first Impressionist exhibition
The female model is Nini Lopez, called 'Fish-Face'
The man on the right is Edmond, the painter's brother
Renoir sold it for 425 francs to pay his rent
Samuel Courtauld acquired it in 1925 for 12,000 pounds

gabrielle-rose.title: Gabrielle with a Rose
descriptions: Gabrielle Renard was the nanny of Renoir's son, Jean
She posed for Renoir for nearly twenty years
Future filmmaker Jean Renoir immortalized her in his memoirs
The painting dates from around 1911, Renoir's late period
The pinkish flesh tones are characteristic of this period

orchestra-opera.title: The Orchestra at the Opera
orchestra-opera.description: Plunging view of the musicians with dancers at the top of the frame.
descriptions: Painted in 1870, Degas depicted his bassoonist friend Désiré Dihau
Composer Emmanuel Chabrier appears in a box on the left
Degas cuts the dancers' bodies at the top of the painting
This innovative composition is inspired by photography
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it in 1894 thanks to the Caillebotte bequest

blue-dancers.title: Blue Dancers
blue-dancers.description: Pastels of dancers adjusting their costumes.
descriptions: This pastel from 1899 is among Degas's last works
His sight failing, he then favored pastel over oil
The strong colors announce the Fauves
Degas brought this pastel from the Pushkin Museum of Modern Art in Moscow
It was exhibited for the first time in 1899 in Paris

dancers-pink-green.title: Dancers, Pink and Green
descriptions: Painted around 1894, this work studies complementary colors
The dancers adjust their costumes backstage
Degas produced over 1,500 works on dancers
He observed the dancers from backstage at the Opéra Garnier
The Metropolitan Museum received it from the Havemeyer bequest in 1929

races-longchamp.title: Races at Longchamp
races-longchamp.description: Jockeys and horses before the race at the Longchamp racecourse.
descriptions: The Longchamp racetrack opened in 1857 in the Bois de Boulogne
Degas was interested in horse movements studied by Muybridge
The jockeys in bright colors punctuate the landscape
Degas painted over 300 works on horse racing
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston holds this canvas

woman-tub.title: Woman in a Tub
woman-tub.description: Female nude bathing, an intimate view from behind.
descriptions: Degas painted and drew over 200 bathers between 1880 and 1900
He said he showed 'the gesture of a woman who thinks she is alone'
This series caused scandal for its raw realism
The dry pastel allowed translucent flesh effects
The Musée d'Orsay preserves several versions of this series

laundresses.title: The Ironers
laundresses.description: Two women at work, one yawning with exhaustion.
descriptions: Painted around 1884, the work shows an ordinary workshop scene
Laundresses were a common subject of social realism
The woman's yawn expresses the physical fatigue of the profession
Émile Zola had just published L'Assommoir on the same milieu
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved the work since 1894

star-dancer.title: The Star
star-dancer.description: Lead dancer taking her bow under the spotlights.
descriptions: This pastel from 1878 captures the moment of the final bow
A man in a black coat can be seen backstage
This man probably represents a protector of the dancer
Degas exploits the overhead view typical of his period
The Étoile is one of the most reproduced works by Degas

bellelli-family.title: The Bellelli Family
bellelli-family.description: Family group portrait with palpable tensions.
descriptions: Degas painted this portrait between 1858 and 1867 during a stay in Florence
The Bellellis are his aunt Laure and his uncle Gennaro
The portrait in the frame depicts his recently deceased grandfather
The painting evokes the couple's tensions in political exile
The Musée d'Orsay acquired this monumental canvas in 1918

boulevard-montmartre-night.title: Boulevard Montmartre at Night
boulevard-montmartre-night.description: Night view of the boulevard lit by gas lamps.
descriptions: Pissarro painted fourteen views of the boulevard from his hotel room
Gas lighting had just been installed in Paris
Pissarro suffered from eye problems and worked from the window
It is his only nocturnal series
The National Gallery in London preserves this unique version

red-roofs.title: The Red Roofs
red-roofs.description: A village seen through winter trees.
descriptions: Painted in 1877 in Pontoise where Pissarro lived
Cézanne and Gauguin came to paint with him in Pontoise
Pissarro was the only painter to exhibit at all eight Impressionist exhibitions
The red roofs contrast with the bare branches of winter
Caillebotte bequeathed it to the French State, displayed today at Orsay

garden-pontoise.title: The Garden at Pontoise
garden-pontoise.description: Vegetable garden with figures at work.
descriptions: Pissarro lived in Pontoise for seventeen years
He preferred to depict cultivated and inhabited landscapes
His palette lightened upon contact with the Impressionists
The Metropolitan Museum in New York preserves this canvas
Pissarro was the elder of the Impressionist group

harvest-pontoise.title: Harvest at Pontoise
harvest-pontoise.description: A rural scene of peasant life.
descriptions: Pissarro defended an anarchist political vision of the rural landscape
He depicted the dignity of peasant work without romanticizing it
The painting dates from 1881 and shows a harvest scene
Pissarro was of Danish origin, born in the West Indies
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved this work since 1947

place-theatre-francais.title: Place du Théâtre Français
place-theatre-francais.museum: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
place-theatre-francais.description: A plunging view of the lively square.
descriptions: Pissarro painted the square from the Hôtel du Louvre in 1898
He created fifteen canvases of this Parisian square
The Comédie-Française is visible in the background
Parisian bustle is rendered through small silhouettes
The Los Angeles County Museum preserves this canvas

peasant-girl-straw-hat.title: Peasant Girl with a Straw Hat
peasant-girl-straw-hat.description: Luminous portrait of a young countrywoman.
descriptions: Painted around 1881, this portrait shows a young peasant from Pontoise
Pissarro was interested in everyday country life
The simple pose attests to his respect for working-class models
The National Gallery of Art in Washington preserves the work
Pissarro would later adopt Seurat's pointillist technique

apple-picking.title: Apple Picking
apple-picking.description: A harvest scene in an orchard.
descriptions: Pissarro painted several orchards during his years in Pontoise
He also painted apple picking in pointillism in the 1880s
Japan was a great admirer of the Impressionists
The Ohara Museum in Kurashiki is Japan's first Western art museum
The museum was founded by textile industrialist Magosaburō Ohara in 1930

flood-port-marly.title: Flood at Port-Marly
flood-port-marly.description: The flooding Seine engulfing the village.
descriptions: Sisley painted seven versions of the Port-Marly flood in 1876
He lived in Marly-le-Roi, west of Paris
The Seine floods were a major event
The sky and water dominate the composition
The Musée d'Orsay preserves the most famous version

snow-louveciennes.title: Snow at Louveciennes
descriptions: Sisley lived in Louveciennes near Versailles
Painted in 1878, the work captures a deserted snowy street
Sisley was an Englishman born and living in France
He would die in poverty in 1899 without having known success
The Musée d'Orsay preserves several winter landscapes by Sisley

bridge-moret.title: The Bridge at Moret
bridge-moret.description: The medieval bridge of the town where Sisley lived.
descriptions: Sisley lived in Moret-sur-Loing for the last twenty years of his life
He painted the medieval bridge more than a dozen times
The bridge dates from the 12th century and still exists today
Sisley always worked outdoors, faithful to Impressionist principles
The Musée d'Orsay preserves this late view by the painter

regatta-molesey.title: Regatta at Molesey
regatta-molesey.description: A boat race on the Thames with flags.
descriptions: Sisley stayed in England during the summer of 1874
The trip was funded by baritone singer Jean-Baptiste Faure
Molesey is located on the Thames near Hampton Court
Sisley only obtained French nationality after his death
The Musée d'Orsay preserves this rare English view

aqueduct-marly.title: The Aqueduct at Marly
aqueduct-marly.description: A monumental structure in the French landscape.
descriptions: The Marly aqueduct was built under Louis XIV to supply Versailles
Sisley lived in Marly-le-Roi at the time of the painting
The contrast between nature and monumental architecture fascinated Sisley
The Toledo Museum of Art has preserved this canvas since 1949
Sisley experienced poverty all his life despite his talent

lane-poplars.title: The Avenue of Poplars at Moret
lane-poplars.description: A row of trees lining a path.
descriptions: Sisley painted several rows of trees bordering the Loing river
The motif of trees in a row creates a dramatic perspective
Cézanne particularly admired Sisley's landscapes
The painting is part of the Caillebotte bequest to the Musée d'Orsay
Sisley remains one of the least recognized Impressionists during his lifetime

child-bath.title: The Child's Bath
child-bath.description: Mother and child in tender intimacy.
descriptions: Mary Cassatt painted this work in 1893, at the peak of her career
Cassatt was the only American to exhibit with the Impressionists
She gave up marriage to devote herself to art
Her palette is inspired by Japanese prints
The Art Institute of Chicago has preserved this work since 1910

little-girl-blue-armchair.title: Little Girl in a Blue Armchair
little-girl-blue-armchair.description: A child slumped in an armchair, an unusual natural pose.
descriptions: Painted in 1878, this portrait shows a sulking little girl
Degas reportedly advised Mary Cassatt on this painting
The slouched pose was revolutionary for child portraiture
The painting was rejected at the American World's Fair of 1878
The National Gallery of Art in Washington acquired it in 1983

tea-cassatt.title: The Tea
tea-cassatt.description: A tea scene between elegant women.
descriptions: Painted around 1880, this work captures a bourgeois social ritual
Cassatt depicts her sister Lydia receiving a friend
The silver tea service belonged to the Cassatt family
Lydia died tragically in 1882 from kidney disease
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston preserves the work

boating-party.title: The Boating Party
boating-party.description: Bold composition with a rower seen from behind.
descriptions: Painted in 1893-1894 during a stay in Antibes on the Riviera
The rower seen from behind recalls Japanese prints
The child in his mother's arms is typical of Cassatt's works
The painting is one of the artist's most reproduced works
The National Gallery of Art in Washington acquired it in 1963

mother-child-cassatt.title: Mother and Child
mother-child-cassatt.description: Mother holding her child in her arms, their faces close together.
descriptions: Cassatt painted hundreds of motherhood scenes
She drew inspiration from Renaissance Madonnas with Child
Her models were often her cousins and their children
She became blind in 1910 and stopped painting
The National Gallery of Art in Washington preserves the work

floor-scrapers.title: The Floor Scrapers
floor-scrapers.description: Workers at work — social realism rare among the Impressionists.
descriptions: Caillebotte painted this scene in 1875
The painting was rejected at the official Salon for its 'vulgar' subject
Caillebotte depicted his own apartment on Boulevard Haussmann
It is one of the first depictions of workers in modern painting
Caillebotte bequeathed his collection to the State, the basis of the Musée d'Orsay

europe-bridge.title: Le Pont de l'Europe
descriptions: Painted in 1876, the bridge spans the tracks of the Saint-Lazare station
The metal bridge was built in 1865
The man on the right is a self-portrait of Caillebotte
The dog represents modern urban loneliness
The Musée du Petit Palais in Geneva holds the work

man-window.title: Young Man at His Window
descriptions: Painted in 1875, this work long belonged to the artist's collection
The observed man is Martial Caillebotte, the painter's brother
The work plays on the urban voyeurism of modernity
Caillebotte lived in opulence thanks to family inheritance
His personal collection of Impressionists enriched the Musée d'Orsay

whistler-mother.title: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1 (Whistler's Mother)
whistler-mother.description: Portrait of the artist's mother that became an American cultural icon.
descriptions: Whistler painted his mother Anna in 1871 in London
The official title emphasizes the harmony of colors
The French State bought it in 1891 for 4,000 francs
It became an icon of Mother's Day in the United States
The work appears in the film Mr Bean at the Cinema

nocturne-blue-gold.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold – Old Battersea Bridge
nocturne-blue-gold.description: Night view of the Thames, with golden reflections in deep blue.
descriptions: Whistler painted several Thames nocturnes around 1872
The term 'nocturne' is borrowed from Chopin's music
It depicts Battersea, then an industrial area of London
The deep blue tone is achieved with Prussian blue
The Tate Britain has preserved this work since 1905

symphony-white-1.title: Symphony in White, No. 1
symphony-white-1.description: Young woman in white on a white rug, a revolutionary tonal harmony.
descriptions: Painted in 1862, the work was rejected by the Paris Salon
It was exhibited at the Salon des Refusés next to Déjeuner sur l'herbe
The model is Joanna Hiffernan, Whistler's Irish mistress
The National Gallery of Art in Washington acquired it in 1943
Whistler liked musical titles for his paintings

nocturne-black-gold.title: Nocturne in Black and Gold – The Falling Rocket
nocturne-black-gold.description: Fireworks at night, painting at the center of the Ruskin-Whistler trial.
descriptions: Painted in 1875, this work caused a famous lawsuit
Critic John Ruskin accused him of 'flinging a pot of paint in the public's face'
Whistler won the trial but received only a symbolic penny
Legal fees ruined him financially
The Detroit Institute of Arts has preserved the work since 1946

starry-night.title: The Starry Night
starry-night.description: Painted from the window of the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, this swirling vision has become a global icon.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this canvas in June 1889 in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence
He painted it from memory in his asylum room
The eleven stars may refer to a passage in Genesis
The depicted village is imaginary, inspired by Northern villages
MoMA in New York acquired it in 1941 for 80,000 dollars

starry-night-rhone.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
starry-night-rhone.description: Night view of the Rhône at Arles with the reflections of gas lights on the water and a couple in the foreground.
descriptions: Painted in September 1888, it is one of the first nocturnal scenes
Van Gogh set up his easel on the banks of the Rhône with candles
The Big Dipper can be seen in the starry sky
The couple in the foreground evokes the lovers of Arles
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it in 1975 through tax-in-kind donations

sunflowers.title: Sunflowers
sunflowers.description: Van Gogh painted this series to decorate Gauguin's room in Arles.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted seven versions of the sunflowers between 1888 and 1889
He wanted to decorate Gauguin's bedroom with these paintings
One version sold for 39.9 million dollars in 1987
The chrome yellow used browns over time, altering the colors
The National Gallery in London preserves the most famous version

cafe-terrace.title: Café Terrace at Night
cafe-terrace.description: The first painting in which Van Gogh uses a starry background, painted outdoors at night.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this scene in September 1888 in Arles
The café was located on Place du Forum and still exists
It is Van Gogh's first starry painting
No black is used in the painting, only blues
The Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo preserves the work

bedroom-arles.title: Bedroom in Arles
bedroom-arles.description: Van Gogh wanted this painting to express 'absolute rest' through its colors.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted three versions of his bedroom between 1888 and 1889
The bedroom was located in the Yellow House, Place Lamartine in Arles
The bright colors were meant to suggest rest and sleep
The self-portraits on the wall depict Van Gogh and his friends
The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam preserves the first version

self-portrait-bandaged-ear.title: Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear
self-portrait-bandaged-ear.description: Painted after he cut off his ear following a quarrel with Gauguin.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this self-portrait in January 1889
The painting was done after the episode when he cut off his ear
The background shows a Japanese print and an empty easel
The pipe symbolizes a certain regained self-control
The Courtauld Gallery in London has preserved the work since 1948

irises.title: Irises
irises.description: Painted a week after his admission to the Saint-Rémy asylum.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted the irises in the asylum garden in May 1889
He considered this painting a 'lightning rod' against his illness
The painting sold for 53.9 million dollars in 1987
Then acquired by the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles in 1990
The isolated white iris in the center creates visual tension

wheatfield-crows.title: Wheatfield with Crows
wheatfield-crows.description: One of Van Gogh's last canvases, often interpreted as premonitory.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this canvas in July 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise
He died less than a month after finishing it
The stormy sky and black crows create an anguished atmosphere
The three diverging paths perhaps symbolize a vital choice
The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam preserves this testamentary work

almond-blossoms.title: Almond Blossom
almond-blossoms.description: Painted to celebrate the birth of his nephew Vincent Willem.
descriptions: Painted in February 1890 in Saint-Rémy for the birth of his nephew
The nephew was named Vincent Willem, like the painter uncle
Van Gogh drew inspiration from Japanese prints of trees in bloom
The intense blue background evokes Provençal winter skies
The painting has become the most beloved work of the Van Gogh Museum

card-players.title: The Card Players
card-players.description: Cézanne painted five versions of this subject, progressively simplifying the composition.
descriptions: Cézanne painted five versions between 1890 and 1896
The models were peasants from the family estate at Jas de Bouffan
One version sold for 250 million dollars to Qatar in 2011
It was then the absolute record for a work of art
The Musée d'Orsay preserves the simplest two-player version

mont-sainte-victoire.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire
mont-sainte-victoire.description: Cézanne painted this Provençal mountain more than 80 times throughout his life.
descriptions: Cézanne painted over 80 versions of this mountain near Aix-en-Provence
He saw in it the pure geological expression of Provence
Its geometric decomposition heralds Cubism
Picasso and Braque intensively studied these paintings
Cézanne died in 1906 from pneumonia caught while painting the mountain

large-bathers-cezanne.title: The Large Bathers
large-bathers-cezanne.description: A monumental masterpiece that influenced Picasso and Matisse.
descriptions: Cézanne worked on this canvas for seven years until his death
It measures over two meters in height
No model posed; Cézanne drew on memories and engravings
The painting directly influenced Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
The Philadelphia Museum of Art acquired it in 1937

still-life-apples.title: Still Life with Apples
still-life-apples.description: Cézanne said he wanted to 'astonish Paris with an apple.'
descriptions: Cézanne painted dozens of still lifes with apples
He said he wanted to 'astonish Paris with an apple'
Apples more solid than reality defy traditional perspective
He observed the fruit for hours to paint them
MoMA in New York preserves several of these works

where-do-we-come-from.title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
where-do-we-come-from.description: Gauguin's artistic testament, painted before a suicide attempt.
descriptions: Gauguin painted this monumental work in 1897 in Tahiti
The canvas measures almost four meters in length
He painted it just before a suicide attempt
The questions in the title can be read in the upper left corner
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston acquired it in 1936

vision-sermon.title: Vision after the Sermon
vision-sermon.description: A break with Impressionism, blending reality and mystical vision.
descriptions: Painted in 1888 during Gauguin's stay in Pont-Aven, Brittany
The painting shows Breton women seeing Jacob wrestling with the angel
The bright red background breaks with Impressionist painting
Gauguin tried to give the painting to the local church, which refused
The Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh acquired it in 1925

arearea.title: Arearea (Joyfulness)
arearea.description: Tahitian scene with bold anti-naturalistic colors.
descriptions: Painted in 1892 during Gauguin's first stay in Tahiti
The Tahitian title means 'amusements' or 'merriment'
The red dog at the bottom of the painting was considered provocative
Gauguin sold the painting to Edgar Degas in 1895
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it in 1961 through the Lung donation

yellow-christ.title: The Yellow Christ
yellow-christ.description: Synthesis of Breton landscape and primitive spirituality.
descriptions: Painted in 1889 in the chapel of Trémalo near Pont-Aven
Gauguin drew inspiration from a 17th-century polychrome wooden Christ
The yellow tone symbolizes the light of Christ for Gauguin
The painting marks the birth of Synthetism
The Albright-Knox Art Gallery in Buffalo acquired it in 1946

sunday-grande-jatte.title: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
sunday-grande-jatte.description: A masterpiece of Pointillism, composed of millions of dots of pure color.
descriptions: Seurat worked two years on this painting from 1884 to 1886
He produced nearly 60 preparatory studies in the open air
The painting contains millions of small dots of pure color
It measures over three meters wide by two meters tall
The Art Institute of Chicago acquired it in 1924 for 24,000 dollars

bathers-asnieres.title: Bathers at Asnières
bathers-asnieres.description: Large composition showing workers bathing in the Seine.
descriptions: Seurat painted this canvas in 1884 at age 24
Asnières was a working-class area northwest of Paris
The painting was rejected by the official Salon of 1884
It was exhibited at the newly created Salon des Indépendants
The National Gallery in London acquired it in 1924

circus.title: The Circus
circus.description: Seurat's last work, unfinished at his death at age 31.
descriptions: Seurat died in March 1891 at just 31 years old
The painting was almost completed at the time of his death
It draws inspiration from the Cirque Fernando at Place Pigalle
The ascending lines convey joy according to Seurat
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it through the John Quinn donation in 1924

moulin-rouge-poster.title: Moulin Rouge: La Goulue
moulin-rouge-poster.description: This poster made Lautrec and the Moulin Rouge famous.
descriptions: Lautrec created this poster in 1891 for the Moulin Rouge
It was his first commercial poster
La Goulue was the cabaret's star, famous for her cancan
The poster was printed in 3,000 copies and plastered throughout Paris
It is preserved at the BnF and the Toulouse-Lautrec Museum in Albi

salon-rue-moulins.title: In the Salon at the Rue des Moulins
salon-rue-moulins.description: Brothel scene treated with humanity and without moral judgment.
descriptions: Lautrec lived several months in Parisian brothels
He painted and drew the residents there without moral judgment
The painting shows the wait before clients arrive
Lautrec donated about fifty works to the Albi museum
The painting dates from 1894 and was exhibited at Goupil in Paris

self-portrait-straw-hat.title: Self-Portrait with a Straw Hat
self-portrait-straw-hat.description: Van Gogh experiments with the divisionist touch of the Impressionists.
descriptions: Painted in Paris during the summer of 1887 during his stay with his brother Theo
Van Gogh painted over 35 self-portraits during his career
He did self-portraits because he could not afford to pay models
The straw hat evokes country painters
The Metropolitan Museum in New York preserves this canvas

self-portrait-grey-hat.title: Self-Portrait with Grey Felt Hat
self-portrait-grey-hat.description: Van Gogh in a grey felt hat, strokes of bright colour on a blue-green background.
descriptions: Painted in winter 1887-1888 just before leaving for Arles
The bright colors herald the chromatic revolution of Arles
Van Gogh discovered Seurat's work just before this self-portrait
The divided brushstrokes recall Neo-Impressionist pointillism
The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam has preserved the work since 1973

self-portrait-1889.title: Self-Portrait, Saint-Rémy
self-portrait-1889.description: Painted at the asylum, with characteristic swirling background.
descriptions: Painted in September 1889 at the Saint-Rémy-de-Provence asylum
It is one of Van Gogh's last self-portraits
The swirling background recalls Starry Night painted at the same time
The work was bought by the French State in 1949
It is displayed at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris

potato-eaters.title: The Potato Eaters
potato-eaters.description: Major work of the Dutch period, with a dark palette.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this canvas in April 1885 in Nuenen, Netherlands
He wanted to show the raw truth of the peasant world
The angular faces were deliberately ugly for Van Gogh
The painting was criticized by his brother Theo for its dark aspect
The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam preserves this major work

night-cafe.title: The Night Café
night-cafe.description: Interior in discordant colors expressing anguish.
descriptions: Painted in September 1888 at the station café in Arles
Van Gogh wrote he wanted to show 'that one can ruin oneself, go mad, commit crimes there'
The violent reds and greens convey human passion
Van Gogh lived three nights in the café to paint it
Yale University Art Gallery has preserved the work since 1961

yellow-house.title: The Yellow House
yellow-house.description: The Arles house where Van Gogh dreamed of a studio of the South.
descriptions: Van Gogh rented this house at 2 Place Lamartine in Arles in May 1888
He lived there from October to December 1888 with Gauguin
The house was destroyed by Allied bombings in 1944
Van Gogh dreamed of founding a 'studio of the South' there with his friends
The Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam preserves the work

langlois-bridge.title: The Langlois Bridge
descriptions: Van Gogh painted the Langlois drawbridge several times in 1888
The bridge reminded Van Gogh of the landscapes of his native Holland
The original bridge was destroyed in 1930 but a replica exists
The bright colors convey the dazzling light of Provence
The Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo preserves this version

olive-trees.title: The Olive Trees
olive-trees.description: Twisted trees under the Provençal sky.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted fifteen olive tree canvases in Saint-Rémy in 1889
He saw them as the rural counterparts of the tormented cypresses
The gnarled trunks seem to dance under the Mistral wind
The yellow-orange ground contrasts with the silvery greens of the olive trees
MoMA in New York preserves this version

cypresses.title: Cypresses
cypresses.description: Cypress trees rising like dark flames.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted the cypresses starting in June 1889 in Saint-Rémy
He wrote that they were 'beautiful as Egyptian obelisks'
The trunks undulate like dark green flames
Cypresses are traditionally planted in Provençal cemeteries
The Metropolitan Museum in New York preserves this canvas

church-auvers.title: The Church at Auvers-sur-Oise
church-auvers.description: Gothic church under a tormented sky.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted the church in June 1890, a month before his death
Auvers-sur-Oise was his last place of residence
He painted the church from the rear, avoiding the banal facade
The intense blue sky contrasts with the distorted architecture
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it in 1951 through the Gachet bequest

dr-gachet.title: Portrait of Dr. Gachet
dr-gachet.description: Man with a melancholy gaze leaning on his fist, a sprig of foxglove beside him.
descriptions: Painted in June 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise by Van Gogh
Dr Gachet was a homeopath and was treating Van Gogh
Gachet was himself an amateur painter and collector
The painting sold for 82.5 million dollars in 1990
It then belonged to Japanese collector Ryoei Saito

portrait-postman.title: Portrait of Postman Roulin
portrait-postman.description: The postman of Arles, Van Gogh's faithful friend.
descriptions: Joseph Roulin was a postman at the Arles station
Van Gogh painted six portraits of him between 1888 and 1889
Roulin agreed to pose for free out of friendship
He supported Van Gogh during his mental crisis in December 1888
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston preserves this version

prisoners-round.title: Prisoners' Round
prisoners-round.description: After an engraving by Gustave Doré — an endless circle.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this scene in February 1890 in Saint-Rémy
He drew inspiration from a Gustave Doré engraving of Newgate prison
The blond prisoner in the center is said to be a self-portrait of Van Gogh
The painting reflects his feeling of confinement at the asylum
The Pushkin Museum in Moscow preserves the work

noon-rest.title: Noonday Rest
noon-rest.description: Peasants asleep in the hay, after Millet.
descriptions: Van Gogh painted this scene in January 1890 in Saint-Rémy
He copied a work by Jean-François Millet whom he admired
Van Gogh used engravings to have models at the asylum
The bright colors transform the Millet original
The Musée d'Orsay preserves the work

bathers-rest.title: Bathers at Rest
bathers-rest.description: Male group in a landscape — a study of volumes.
descriptions: Cézanne painted several bather studies around 1876-1877
He drew inspiration from compositions by Poussin and the Renaissance
Cézanne could not have nude models pose outdoors
He used photographs and his memories
The Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia preserves this work

house-hanged-man.title: The House of the Hanged Man
house-hanged-man.description: Landscape of Auvers shown at the first Impressionist exhibition.
descriptions: Cézanne painted this house in Auvers-sur-Oise in 1873
Pissarro lived nearby and advised Cézanne
The painting was exhibited at the first Impressionist exhibition of 1874
It was bought by Count Doria for 300 francs
The Musée d'Orsay acquired it in 1911 through the Camondo bequest

blue-vase.title: The Blue Vase
blue-vase.description: Still life of flowers in a blue vase.
descriptions: Cézanne painted this still life around 1889-1890
The vase, the apple and the orange were his favorite objects
Cézanne liked to build his compositions through geometric planes
The work entered the Musée d'Orsay in 1911 through the Camondo bequest
The deep blue of the vase contrasts with the orange fruit

baskets-apples.title: The Basket of Apples
baskets-apples.description: Deliberately unbalanced still life, a new perspective.
descriptions: Cézanne painted this still life around 1893
The tilted basket deliberately defies the laws of perspective
Cézanne preferred apples because they did not spoil quickly
The work was acquired by Auguste Pellerin, great collector
The Art Institute of Chicago has preserved it since 1926

bibemus-quarries.title: The Bibémus Quarries
descriptions: Cézanne rented a cabin at the Bibémus quarries in 1895
The quarries provided the ocher stone for the buildings of Aix-en-Provence
The natural geometry of the rocks fascinated the painter
Picasso visited this site to understand Cézanne
The Museum Folkwang in Essen preserves this work

gardanne.title: Gardanne
gardanne.description: Provençal village reduced to its geometric forms.
descriptions: Cézanne lived in Gardanne in 1885-1886 after his marriage
He painted several views of the hilltop village there
The painting reduces the village to cubes and prisms
This geometrization deeply influenced Cubism
The Metropolitan Museum in New York preserves the work

lac-annecy.title: Lake Annecy
lac-annecy.description: View of the lake from the Château de Duingt.
descriptions: Cézanne stayed in Talloires on Lake Annecy in July 1896
The visible Duingt castle dates from the 12th century
He found the landscape too 'idyllic' for his taste
The painting was bought by Egisto Fabbri, Italian collector
The Courtauld Gallery in London has preserved it since 1932

madame-cezanne-red.title: Madame Cézanne in a Red Dress
madame-cezanne-red.description: Portrait of his wife Hortense, in an austere pose.
descriptions: Cézanne painted his wife Hortense Fiquet nearly thirty times
This version dates from 1888-1890
Hortense had to pose for hours without moving for Cézanne
The couple married in 1886 after sixteen years of relationship
The Metropolitan Museum in New York preserves this work

boy-red-vest.title: Boy in a Red Vest
boy-red-vest.description: Portrait of an Italian model, with distorted arms.
descriptions: Cézanne painted this canvas in 1888 in his Parisian studio
The model is named Michelangelo di Rosa, a young Italian
One version was stolen in 2008 from the Bührle Foundation in Zurich
It was recovered in Serbia in 2012 after four years
The painting is one of Cézanne's most reproduced works

manao-tupapau.title: Manao tupapau (Spirit of the Dead Watching)
descriptions: Gauguin painted this canvas in 1892 during his first stay in Tahiti
The model is his young companion Teha'amana, age 13
The title refers to Tahitian ancestral spirits
Gauguin drew inspiration from Manet's Olympia, reversing the pose
The Albright-Knox Art Gallery in Buffalo preserves the work

two-tahitian-women.title: Two Tahitian Women
two-tahitian-women.description: Portrait of two women carrying fruit.
descriptions: Painted in 1899 during Gauguin's second stay in Polynesia
The women carry traditional mango fruit
The painting evokes the simple and harmonious beauty of nature
The Metropolitan Museum in New York acquired it in 1949
Gauguin idealized Tahiti as a paradise lost in the West

ia-orana-maria.title: Ia Orana Maria
descriptions: Painted in 1891, the title means 'Hail Mary' in Tahitian
Gauguin transposes Christian iconography into a Polynesian setting
The yellow angel in the background recalls Gabriel of the Annunciation
The painting marks the religious syncretism dear to Gauguin
The Met in New York acquired it through the Havemeyer bequest in 1951

when-marry.title: When Will You Marry?
when-marry.description: Two Tahitian women in a tropical landscape, one in traditional dress, the other in Western clothes.
descriptions: Painted in 1892 during his first stay in Tahiti
The painting sold for around 300 million dollars in 2014
The record sale was concluded between the Staechelin family and Qatar
The Tahitian title Nafea Faa Ipoipo questions marriage
Gauguin contrasts a traditional young woman with another in Western dress

te-rerioa.title: Te Rerioa (The Dream)
descriptions: Painted in 1897 during Gauguin's second stay in Tahiti
The title means 'the dream' or 'the nightmare' in Tahitian
The wall sculptures evoke Polynesian deities
The sleeping baby in the cradle is peaceful and enigmatic
The Courtauld Gallery in London has preserved the work since 1934

vahine-mango.title: Vahine no te vi (Woman with a Mango)
vahine-mango.description: Portrait of a Tahitian woman holding a fruit.
descriptions: Painted in 1892, this portrait shows Teha'amana, Gauguin's companion
The pose mirrors that of a Christian Virgin and Child
The mango symbolizes fertility and tropical abundance
The Baltimore Museum of Art acquired it in 1950
Gauguin was then forty-four years old, his model thirteen

self-portrait-halo.title: Self-Portrait with Halo
self-portrait-halo.description: Gauguin depicts himself as a saint or a demon.
descriptions: Painted in 1889 at Marie Henry's boarding house at Le Pouldu in Brittany
The halo and the snake symbolize the dual aspect of the artist
The apples evoke temptation and original sin
The painting decorated the boarding house dining room
The National Gallery of Art in Washington preserves it

bonjour-monsieur-gauguin.title: Bonjour Monsieur Gauguin
bonjour-monsieur-gauguin.description: Gauguin in a dark coat greeting a Breton peasant woman in front of a gate.
descriptions: Painted in 1889, Gauguin pays homage to Bonjour Monsieur Courbet
The author of the famous original painting is Gustave Courbet
Gauguin depicts himself traveling on foot with his hat and stick
The Breton peasant woman greets him in a rural scene
The Prague Museum of Modern Art has preserved it since 1923

tahitian-women-beach.title: Tahitian Women on the Beach
tahitian-women-beach.description: Two seated women, a serene composition.
descriptions: Painted in 1891 at the beginning of Gauguin's first Tahitian stay
The painting evokes the serenity of the South Pacific
The bright colors contrast with the pinkish sand of the beach
Gauguin sold this painting upon his return to Paris in 1893
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved it since 1923 through the Brunecker bequest

nevermore.title: Nevermore
nevermore.description: Reclining nude with a raven, a reference to Edgar Allan Poe.
descriptions: Painted in 1897 during his second stay in Tahiti
The title is borrowed from Edgar Allan Poe's poem The Raven
The perched raven evokes a disturbing presence
Gauguin sold the painting to composer Frederick Delius
The Courtauld Gallery in London has preserved it since 1932

models.title: Les Poseuses
models.description: Three models in the studio with La Grande Jatte in the background.
descriptions: Seurat painted this canvas between 1886 and 1888
La Grande Jatte can be recognized hanging on the studio wall
A single model posed for the three figures, seen from front, back and profile
The painting measures over two meters in height
The Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia has preserved it since 1926

chahut.title: Le Chahut
chahut.description: Cabaret dance with joyful upward lines.
descriptions: Painted in 1889-1890, it is Seurat's penultimate major work
The chahut was a cabaret dance preceding the cancan
Seurat applies his theory of joyful ascending lines
The scene takes place at the Divan Japonais in Paris
The Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo preserves the work

gravelines-channel.title: The Channel at Gravelines
descriptions: Seurat painted this seascape during the summer of 1890 in Gravelines
It is his last productive summer before his premature death
He painted four views of the channel and the coast there
The pale colors contrast with his previous canvases
The National Gallery in London preserves this work

palace-popes.title: Palais des Papes at Avignon
palace-popes.description: Medieval architecture in a mosaic of colors.
descriptions: Signac painted the Palace of the Popes in 1900 during a stay in Avignon
The palace was the residence of the popes in the 14th century
Signac inherited the pointillist technique from his friend Seurat
His brushstroke widened into a bright colored mosaic
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved the work since 1947

port-saint-tropez.title: The Port of Saint-Tropez
descriptions: Signac discovered Saint-Tropez in 1892 and settled there
He introduced the village to the Fauves and Matisse
Signac had bought the house La Hune on the port
The painting dates from around 1901-1902
The Museum of Western Art in Tokyo preserves it

pine-tree-saint-tropez.title: The Pine Tree, Saint-Tropez
descriptions: Painted around 1909, this pine was the subject of numerous studies
Signac considered this tree a personal signature
The umbrella pine is typical of Mediterranean landscapes
The Pushkin Museum in Moscow preserves this work
The bright colors reflect the evolution toward late Divisionism

jane-avril-dancing.title: Jane Avril Dancing
jane-avril-dancing.description: The famous dancer in full performance.
descriptions: Jane Avril was a star dancer at the Moulin Rouge
Nicknamed 'La Mélinite', she danced a more sophisticated cancan
Lautrec produced several posters and portraits of her
The painting dates from 1892 and captures her singular grace
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved it since 1949

at-moulin-rouge.title: At the Moulin Rouge
at-moulin-rouge.description: Night scene with a green face lit from below.
descriptions: Painted between 1892 and 1895 at the famous Pigalle cabaret
La Goulue can be recognized in the background fixing her hair
The green face in the foreground belongs to May Milton, a dancer
Lautrec himself appears on the right, small and hatted
The Art Institute of Chicago has preserved it since 1928

divan-japonais.title: Divan Japonais
descriptions: Lithographic poster produced by Lautrec in 1892-1893
The Divan Japonais was a café-concert on Rue des Martyrs
Jane Avril can be recognized as a spectator in the foreground
Singer Yvette Guilbert appears on stage, deliberately headless
The poster has become iconic of Belle Époque Paris

aristide-bruant.title: Aristide Bruant in His Cabaret
aristide-bruant.description: Iconic poster of the singer with red scarf.
descriptions: Aristide Bruant was a famous singer at the Le Mirliton cabaret
The red scarf and black hat were his signature
Lautrec produced several posters for Bruant between 1892 and 1894
Bruant demanded the poster for his provincial tours
The flat color areas influenced 20th-century poster artists

nude-bath.title: Nude in the Bath
nude-bath.description: Woman lying in a bathtub, warm and luminous colours.
descriptions: Bonnard painted his companion Marthe bathing for thirty years
Marthe suffered from an illness that forced her to wash frequently
The painting captures the light bouncing off the mosaic
Bonnard painted from memory, never in front of the model
The Paris Museum of Modern Art preserves this work

dining-room-country.title: The Dining Room in the Country
dining-room-country.description: Luminous interior with view of the garden.
descriptions: Painted in 1913 at Bonnard's house in Vernonnet in Normandy
The window opens onto nature, a recurring motif in Bonnard's work
Marthe and a cat can be seen in the room
Bonnard sought to merge interior and exterior
The Minneapolis Institute of Art has preserved this work since 1954

white-cat.title: The White Cat
descriptions: Painted in 1894, this painting was 27 when it entered the Luxembourg
Bonnard loved cats and often painted them
The caricatural elongation of the legs is deliberately decorative
The flat style is inspired by Japanese prints
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved the work since 1947

jardins-publics.title: Public Gardens
descriptions: Vuillard painted this series of decorative panels in 1894
They were intended for the dining room of Alexandre Natanson
Vuillard was a member of the Nabis group founded in 1888
The floral and fragmented motifs recall tapestries
The Musée d'Orsay preserves several of these panels

elegante-vuillard.title: The Elegant Woman
elegante-vuillard.description: Woman in a bourgeois interior with abundant decorative motifs.
descriptions: Vuillard makes the figure disappear into the overloaded decor
His technique mixes glue paint and impasto
Vuillard lived with his dressmaker mother who often posed
He frequented the Nabi circle with Bonnard and Maurice Denis
The Musée d'Orsay preserves several Vuillard interiors

seamstresses-vuillard.title: The Seamstresses
seamstresses-vuillard.description: An intimate scene from the daily life of his seamstress mother.
descriptions: Vuillard's mother ran a sewing workshop in their apartment
Vuillard painted dozens of intimate workshop scenes
