The fabric patterns mingle with the wallpaper
This technique foreshadows abstract research
Vuillard collaborated with La Revue blanche, a symbolist journal

the-dream-rousseau.title: The Dream
the-dream-rousseau.description: Rousseau's last major work, a dreamlike jungle with a nude woman on a couch.
descriptions: Painted in 1910, a few months before Rousseau's death
The painting measures over two meters in height
The nude woman represents Yadwigha, a Polish youthful love
Rousseau never left France and imagined the jungle
MoMA in New York acquired it in 1954 for 10,000 dollars

sleeping-gypsy.title: The Sleeping Gypsy
sleeping-gypsy.description: A lion contemplating a sleeping gypsy under the moon, a poetic and mysterious vision.
descriptions: Painted in 1897 by Rousseau, a Parisian customs official
The painting was rejected by the Laval city hall and remained unknown
It was rediscovered by Picasso in 1923 at a junk dealer's
MoMA in New York acquired it in 1939
The lion and mandolin create a memorable dreamlike scene

snake-charmer.title: The Snake Charmer
snake-charmer.description: Silhouette playing the flute in a lush jungle in the moonlight.
descriptions: Painted in 1907 for the mother of painter Robert Delaunay
Rousseau drew inspiration from the Jardin des Plantes for his jungles
He read travel descriptions and looked at postcards
The black silhouette evokes the mysteries of Oriental tales
The Musée d'Orsay has preserved the work since 1923 through the Delaunay bequest

liberty-leading.title: Liberty Leading the People
liberty-leading.description: Symbol of the French Republic, this painting commemorates the Trois Glorieuses of July 1830.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in a few months at the end of 1830
It commemorates the Three Glorious Days of 27, 28 and 29 July 1830
Marianne, with bare breast, brandishes the tricolor flag
The child with pistols reportedly inspired Gavroche to Victor Hugo
The Louvre has preserved the canvas since 1874

death-sardanapalus.title: The Death of Sardanapalus
death-sardanapalus.description: A scene of orgiastic destruction inspired by Byron that caused a scandal at the Salon.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1827 after a play by Lord Byron
The Assyrian king Sardanapalus has everything he owns slaughtered
The painting caused scandal at the Salon of 1827
The diagonals and sensuality foreshadow Romantic Baroque
The Louvre acquired it in 1921 for 700,000 francs

women-algiers.title: Women of Algiers in Their Apartment
women-algiers.description: A memory of Delacroix's trip to Morocco, which would influence Renoir and Picasso.
descriptions: Painted in 1834 after Delacroix's trip to Morocco in 1832
Delacroix visited a harem in Algiers, a rare thing for a Westerner
The painting inspired Picasso's Women of Algiers a century later
Picasso produced fifteen variations on the Delacroix painting
The Louvre has preserved the original work since 1874

raft-medusa.title: The Raft of the Medusa
raft-medusa.description: This monumental painting denounces the shipwreck caused by the incompetence of a captain appointed through favoritism.
descriptions: Géricault painted the canvas between 1818 and 1819 at age 28
It evokes the shipwreck of the frigate La Méduse in 1816
147 people were abandoned on a raft, 15 survived
Géricault interviewed survivors and visited morgues
The painting measures five meters by seven at the Louvre

charging-chasseur.title: The Charging Chasseur
charging-chasseur.description: Géricault's first success, which stages Napoleonic heroism.
descriptions: Géricault painted this canvas at 21 in just a few weeks
Presented at the Salon of 1812, it secured his fame
The rearing horse foreshadows Romantic energy
Géricault was fascinated by horses all his life
He would die in 1824 at 32 from a horse fall

rain-steam-speed.title: Rain, Steam and Speed
rain-steam-speed.description: A train crossing a misty landscape, an almost abstract vision of modernity.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1844 on the Great Western Railway line
A hare can barely be made out running in front of the train
The depicted bridge is the Maidenhead Railway Bridge
Turner reportedly observed the landscape through the window in the storm
The National Gallery in London has preserved the work since 1856

fighting-temeraire.title: The Fighting Temeraire
fighting-temeraire.description: Voted 'greatest British painting' in 2005, it shows the end of the age of sail.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1839 at age 64
The Temeraire had fought at Trafalgar in 1805
The ship is being towed by a steamboat for demolition
The painting symbolizes the passage from the age of sail to steam
Voted favorite of the British in 2005 by the BBC

slave-ship.title: The Slave Ship
slave-ship.description: Poignant denunciation of the slave trade through an apocalyptic storm.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1840 to denounce slavery
It evokes the Zong massacre in 1781 when 132 slaves were thrown into the sea
John Ruskin wrote that it was the most beautiful seascape ever painted
Turner sought to provoke British parliamentary debate
The Museum of Fine Arts Boston has preserved the work since 1899

wanderer-sea-fog.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
wanderer-sea-fog.description: Icon of German Romanticism, man facing the immensity of nature.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas around 1818 in southern Germany
The traveler seen from behind invites the viewer to identify with him
The mountains perhaps represent the Elbsandsteingebirge
It has become the emblematic image of German Romanticism
The Hamburg Kunsthalle has preserved it since 1970

monk-sea.title: The Monk by the Sea
monk-sea.description: Absolute solitude before the infinite, a revolutionary painting in its starkness.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas between 1808 and 1810
The tiny monk before the immensity creates a dizzying effect
The painting shocked with its extreme austerity at the Berlin Salon
Heinrich von Kleist wrote a famous text about the work
The Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin has preserved it since 1906

abbey-oakwood.title: The Abbey in the Oakwood
abbey-oakwood.description: Funeral procession in Gothic ruins, a meditation on death and faith.
descriptions: Painted between 1808 and 1810 as a counterpart to The Monk by the Sea
Friedrich depicts the ruins of Eldena Abbey in Pomerania
The painting evokes death, faith and nature reclaiming its rights
The bare oaks accompany the funeral procession
The Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin has preserved it since 1906

ice-sea.title: The Sea of Ice
ice-sea.description: A ship crushed by the ice, a metaphor for the failure of human ambition.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas in 1823-1824
It draws inspiration from William Edward Parry's expedition to the Arctic
The crushed ship symbolizes shattered human hopes
The painting was seen as a political protest against the Reaction
The Hamburg Kunsthalle preserves it

third-may.title: The Third of May 1808
third-may.description: Denunciation of the executions of Spanish resistance fighters by Napoleonic troops.
descriptions: Goya painted this canvas in 1814 to commemorate Spanish resistance
The scene takes place in Madrid on the night of 3 May 1808
The man in the white shirt evokes the crucified Christ
Picasso and Manet drew inspiration from it for their own paintings
The Prado Museum in Madrid has preserved it since 1873

saturn-son.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
saturn-son.description: One of the 'Black Paintings' made by Goya on the walls of his house.
descriptions: Goya painted this work around 1820-1823 on the wall of his house
It is one of the fourteen 'black paintings' from the Quinta del Sordo
They were transferred to canvas starting in 1874
Goya suffered from deafness and psychological troubles
The Prado Museum has preserved them since 1881

maja-desnuda.title: The Nude Maja
maja-desnuda.description: The first Spanish female nude showing pubic hair, commissioned for a private collection.
descriptions: Goya painted this canvas between 1797 and 1800 for Manuel Godoy
Godoy was the prime minister of King Charles IV of Spain
The model's identity remains a controversial mystery
The Inquisition summoned Goya because of this nude
The Prado Museum in Madrid preserves the work

sleep-reason.title: The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters
sleep-reason.description: Emblematic etching of Los Caprichos, a critique of obscurantism.
descriptions: This engraving from 1799 is part of the Caprichos series
The full title specifies 'united with reason, imagination creates wonders'
Owls, bats and lynxes surround the sleeping artist
Goya criticizes the vices and superstition of his time
The series of 80 prints was self-published

shipwreck-turner.title: The Shipwreck
shipwreck-turner.description: A maritime drama with rescue amid raging waves.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1805 at age 30
It is his first major shipwreck scene
The painting established him as the master of British seascape
The swirling waves foreshadow his later works
The Tate Britain in London preserves the work

burning-parliament.title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons
descriptions: Turner painted several versions of the 16 October 1834 fire
He sketched the scene live from the Thames
The fire lasted all night and attracted an immense crowd
Charles Barry rebuilt Parliament in his Neo-Gothic style
The Philadelphia Museum of Art preserves one version

regulus-turner.title: Regulus
regulus-turner.description: Blinding light symbolizing the torment of the Roman general.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1828 then reworked it in 1837
The Roman general Regulus had his eyelids cut off by the Carthaginians
Turner conveys the blinding light of the sun
The viewer is put in the place of the condemned man
The Tate Britain preserves this work

dido-carthage.title: Dido Building Carthage
dido-carthage.description: Luminous vision of the ancient city.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1815 inspired by Claude Lorrain
He considered Claude his great landscape model
Turner bequeathed the painting to the National Gallery on condition it be hung next to a Claude
This condition is still respected today
The work symbolizes the painter's artistic rivalry with his predecessors

snowstorm-steamboat.title: Snow Storm – Steam-Boat off a Harbour's Mouth
snowstorm-steamboat.description: Turner reportedly asked to be tied to the mast to observe.
descriptions: Turner painted this canvas in 1842 at age 67
The artist claimed to have had himself tied to the mast of a boat
No evidence was found of this storm voyage
The painting foreshadows abstraction through its dissolution of forms
The Tate Britain has preserved the work since the Turner bequest

chalk-cliffs-rugen.title: Chalk Cliffs on Rügen
chalk-cliffs-rugen.description: Three figures contemplating the vertiginous cliffs.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas in 1818 during his honeymoon
The island of Rügen is famous for its white chalk cliffs
The woman depicted is Caroline, his recent wife
The painter's brother also appears contemplating the scene
The Oskar Reinhart Museum in Winterthur preserves the work

woman-rising-sun.title: Woman before the Rising Sun
woman-rising-sun.description: Female silhouette facing the rosy dawn.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas around 1818-1820
The woman raises her arms in a mystical gesture toward the dawn
The motif evokes prayer or communion with nature
The Museum Folkwang in Essen preserves the work
The museum was founded in 1902 and has a rich Romantic collection

moonrise-sea.title: Moonrise over the Sea
moonrise-sea.description: Figures contemplating the moon above the waves.
descriptions: Friedrich painted several versions of this scene between 1821 and 1822
The three seated figures evoke collective meditation
Moonlight on the waves fascinated the Romantics
Friedrich considered the moon a symbol of life after death
The Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin preserves this work

tree-crows.title: The Tree of Crows
tree-crows.description: A tormented oak under a dramatic sky.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas around 1822
The prehistoric burial mound under the oak evokes death
The twisted tree symbolizes resistance to time
Friedrich often painted from his memories of the Baltic
The Louvre acquired it in 1975, a rare German Romantic work at the museum

two-men-moon.title: Two Men Contemplating the Moon
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas in 1819-1820
The two men are said to be Friedrich and his disciple August Heinrich
They wear the old German costume banned after 1819
The painting may contain implicit political criticism
The Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Dresden preserves it

winter-landscape.title: Winter Landscape with a Church
winter-landscape.description: A man at prayer near snow-covered firs.
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas in 1811
The praying man has abandoned his crutches, perhaps a miracle
The Gothic church evokes spiritual salvation
The painting is a hymn to the Christian faith
The National Gallery in London has preserved it since 1987

sunset-brothers.title: Sunset (Brothers)
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas around 1830-1835
The two silhouettes are said to be Friedrich and his brother
Twilight is a recurring theme of German Romanticism
Catherine the Great had initiated the French collection of the Hermitage Museum
The Hermitage in Saint Petersburg preserves this work

giant-mountains.title: Morning in the Giant Mountains
descriptions: Friedrich painted this canvas around 1810-1820
The Giant Mountains are on the Polish-Czech border
Friedrich had taken a hiking trip there in 1810
The misty peaks create a mystical atmosphere
The Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin preserves the work

hay-wain.title: The Hay Wain
hay-wain.description: An English rural scene that became an icon of landscape painting.
descriptions: Constable painted this canvas in 1821 at age 45
The scene takes place at Flatford in his native Suffolk
The painting won the gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824
It deeply influenced Delacroix and French landscape painters
The National Gallery in London acquired it in 1886

salisbury-cathedral-meadows.title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Meadows
salisbury-cathedral-meadows.description: A masterpiece of light and clouds.
descriptions: Constable painted this canvas in 1831 at age 55
His wife Maria had just died, the painting expresses his grief
The rainbow symbolizes religious hope
The painting was bought in 2013 by the National Gallery
It had been funded by 19 million pounds of public subscription

dedham-vale.title: Dedham Vale
dedham-vale.description: The Suffolk valley he painted throughout his life.
descriptions: Constable painted his first version of Dedham Vale in 1802
He returned to this landscape throughout his career
Dedham Vale was the region of his childhood in Suffolk
Constable said he had made every corner his own
The Victoria and Albert Museum preserves several versions

flatford-mill.title: Flatford Mill
flatford-mill.description: His father's mill on the River Stour.
descriptions: Constable painted this canvas in 1816-1817 at age 40
Flatford Mill belonged to his father Golding Constable
It is Constable's first major six-foot landscape
The painting found no buyer during his lifetime
The Tate Britain has preserved it since 1854

leaping-horse.title: The Leaping Horse
leaping-horse.description: A barge-towing scene on the canal.
descriptions: Constable painted this canvas in 1825 at age 49
It shows a barge horse leaping over a canal barrier
It is one of his six great animated six-foot landscapes
Constable made numerous successive modifications to it
The Royal Academy of Arts has preserved the work since his bequest in 1875

cloud-study.title: Cloud Study
cloud-study.description: One of Constable's many sky studies.
descriptions: Constable produced nearly 100 sky studies between 1821 and 1822
He painted them on the back of engravings, outdoors at Hampstead
He noted on the back the hour, wind and weather conditions
Constable considered himself a 'landscape meteorologist'
The Victoria and Albert Museum preserves the majority of them

stonehenge-constable.title: Stonehenge
stonehenge-constable.description: The megalithic monument under a stormy sky.
descriptions: Constable painted this watercolor around 1835
He visited Stonehenge in 1820 and 1835
The stormy sky and double rainbows evoke drama
Constable said the stones were 'immeasurably ancient'
The Victoria and Albert Museum preserves the work

cornfield.title: The Cornfield
cornfield.description: A shaded path leading to golden fields.
descriptions: Constable painted this canvas in 1826 at age 50
The painting shows the path to the school he took as a child
It was bought by subscription for the National Gallery in 1837
Constable died the same year at age 60
The donkey and the drinking child represent rural innocence

massacre-chios.title: The Massacre at Chios
massacre-chios.description: Denunciation of Turkish atrocities in Greece.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1824 at age 26
It evokes the massacre of the Greek island of Chios in 1822
The Ottomans had massacred 20,000 Orthodox Greeks
The work was nicknamed 'the massacre of painting' by Gros
The Louvre acquired it the very year of its creation

medea-delacroix.title: Medea about to Kill Her Children
medea-delacroix.description: The sorceress about to kill her children.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1838 at age 40
Medea is about to kill her children in revenge against Jason
The subject comes from the tragedy by Euripides
The shadows on Medea's face convey her torment
The Louvre has preserved the work since 1874

greece-ruins-missolonghi.title: Greece on the Ruins of Missolonghi
greece-ruins-missolonghi.description: Allegory of Greece after the heroic siege.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1826
It commemorates the heroic siege of Missolonghi by the Turks in 1826
Lord Byron had taken part and died there in 1824
The work was sold for the benefit of Greek fighters
The Bordeaux Museum of Fine Arts has preserved it since 1851

orphan-cemetery.title: Young Orphan in the Cemetery
orphan-cemetery.description: Moving portrait of a young girl in mourning.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1824 as a study for the Massacre of Chios
The painting was finally exhibited separately at the Salon
The large moist eyes express silent distress
The painting was bought by the French State in 1874
The Louvre preserves it in the 19th-century paintings collection

lion-hunt-delacroix.title: Lion Hunt
lion-hunt-delacroix.description: An animal-violence scene inspired by Rubens.
descriptions: Delacroix painted several versions of lion hunts between 1854 and 1861
Part of the Bordeaux painting was destroyed by a fire in 1870
He drew inspiration from Rubens's hunts which he admired
The bright colors influenced Renoir and Monet
The Bordeaux Museum of Fine Arts preserves this fragmentary work

entry-crusaders.title: The Entry of the Crusaders in Constantinople
entry-crusaders.description: The Fourth Crusade and the sack of the Byzantine city.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this canvas in 1840
It evokes the capture of Constantinople by the Crusaders in 1204
The painting was commissioned for the Versailles Historical Museum
It was transferred to the Louvre in 1885
Delacroix criticizes the violence of the Crusaders despite the official commission

hamlet-horatio.title: Hamlet and Horatio in the Graveyard
hamlet-horatio.description: A Shakespeare scene with Yorick's skull.
descriptions: Delacroix painted this scene in 1839
It illustrates Act V of Shakespeare's play
Yorick's skull recalls the ephemeral nature of life
Shakespeare was a major source of inspiration for the Romantics
The Louvre has preserved the work since 1874

clothed-maja.title: The Clothed Maja
clothed-maja.description: Woman reclining on cushions in a white dress and short jacket, looking straight ahead.
descriptions: Goya painted this canvas between 1800 and 1807, the counterpart to the Naked Maja
The same model poses in the same position, but dressed
Manuel Godoy owned both paintings in his collection
The Inquisition questioned Goya about the model's identity
Goya refused to answer; the Prado preserves both works

family-charles-iv.title: The Family of Charles IV
family-charles-iv.description: Unsparing group portrait of the royal family.
descriptions: Goya painted this group portrait in 1800
He depicted himself in the shadows on the left, like Velázquez
The portrait shows the royal family without any flattery
Théophile Gautier described it as 'the corner baker with his wife'
The Prado Museum in Madrid preserves the work

colossus.title: The Colossus
colossus.description: A giant dominating a landscape of panicked flight.
descriptions: The Colossus has long been attributed to Goya
Recent research attributes it to his student Asensio Juliá
The painting dates from around 1808-1812 during the war
The giant perhaps symbolizes Spanish resistance
The Prado Museum preserves the work in the Goya section

witches-sabbath.title: Witches' Sabbath
witches-sabbath.description: Black painting showing a diabolical goat preaching.
descriptions: This 1820-1823 black painting adorned Goya's dining room
The large black goat represents Satan presiding over the sabbath
Goya painted directly on the plaster wall
The works were transferred to canvas between 1874 and 1878
The Prado Museum received them as a donation in 1881

dog-goya.title: The Dog
dog-goya.description: Enigmatic Black Painting — a dog's head emerging.
descriptions: This black painting is one of Goya's most enigmatic
The almost submerged dog evokes drowning or being trapped
No definitive interpretation exists to date
The image foreshadows abstraction through its strange emptiness
The Prado Museum preserves this work

pilgrimage-san-isidro.title: Pilgrimage to San Isidro
pilgrimage-san-isidro.description: A grimacing crowd in a Black Painting.
descriptions: This 1820-1823 black painting shows deformed pilgrims
Goya had painted a joyful San Isidro Meadow 30 years earlier
The contrast between the two works marks his disillusionment
The grimacing faces evoke decadent humanity
The Prado Museum preserves all the black paintings

shootings-third-may.title: El tres de mayo
shootings-third-may.description: The executions of May 3, 1808, an icon of resistance.
descriptions: Goya painted this monumental painting in 1814
The Spanish title El tres de mayo en Madrid specifies the place and date
The scene evokes the French repression of the 1808 uprising
Manet drew inspiration from it for his Execution of Maximilian
The Prado Museum has preserved it since 1872

mad-woman-envy.title: The Insane Woman (Envy)
mad-woman-envy.description: Psychiatric portrait of a mentally ill woman.
descriptions: Géricault painted ten portraits of the insane around 1820-1824
Five portraits have been recovered to date
Dr. Étienne-Jean Georget commissioned these works for his studies
Géricault was himself psychologically fragile
The Lyon Museum of Fine Arts preserves this canvas

mad-man-kidnapping.title: The Kleptomaniac
mad-man-kidnapping.description: Revolutionary series of portraits of mental patients.
descriptions: Géricault painted this portrait around 1822-1823
The subject suffers from monomania of theft according to Dr. Georget
'Monomania' is a 19th-century psychiatric notion
Géricault treats his models with dignity and humanity
The Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent preserves this canvas

derby-epsom.title: The Epsom Derby
derby-epsom.description: Horse race with horses caught in suspended gallop.
descriptions: Géricault painted this canvas in 1821 during a stay in London
The suspended gallop was considered erroneous
Eadweard Muybridge would later prove that the gallop is different
Géricault drew inspiration from the English prints of the time
The Louvre has preserved this canvas since 1865

horse-frightened-lightning.title: Horse Frightened by Lightning
descriptions: Géricault painted this canvas around 1813-1814 at age 22
The rearing horse expresses primal terror
Géricault was passionate about horses all his life
He died in 1824 from the consequences of a horse fall
The National Gallery in London preserves this canvas

wounded-cuirassier.title: Wounded Cuirassier Leaving the Battle
wounded-cuirassier.description: Wounded officer moving away from the battlefield — the end of the Napoleonic epic.
descriptions: Géricault painted this canvas in 1814 at age 23
It was presented at the Salon at the same time as the Wounded Cuirassier
The pose contrasts with the victorious surge of his Officer of 1812
The painting expresses the melancholy of Napoleonic defeat
The Louvre has preserved the work since 1851

blue-boy.title: The Blue Boy
blue-boy.description: Iconic portrait of a young man in a blue satin costume, an homage to Van Dyck.
descriptions: Gainsborough painted The Blue Boy around 1770
The model is said to be Jonathan Buttall, the son of a wealthy merchant
The blue satin costume pays homage to Van Dyck's portraits
The work has become an American cultural icon
The Huntington Library in California has preserved it since 1921

mr-mrs-andrews.title: Mr and Mrs Andrews
mr-mrs-andrews.description: Double portrait in a Suffolk landscape, a fusion of portrait and landscape.
descriptions: Gainsborough painted this double portrait around 1750
He was then only 22 years old
Robert and Frances Andrews had just married
The Andrews owned the Suffolk lands visible on the right
The National Gallery in London acquired it in 1960

morning-walk.title: The Morning Walk
morning-walk.description: Elegant couple walking with their dog in a park.
descriptions: Gainsborough painted this canvas in 1785
The subjects are William Hallett and Elizabeth Stephen, newlyweds
The spitz dog in the foreground adds a tender touch
The portrait was painted just after their marriage
The National Gallery in London has preserved the work since 1954

mrs-siddons-gainsborough.title: Portrait of Mrs Siddons
mrs-siddons-gainsborough.description: The famous tragic actress in elegant city attire.
descriptions: Gainsborough painted Sarah Siddons in 1785
She was the greatest tragedian of her time
The red feathered hat contrasts with the blue striped coat
Gainsborough painted the portrait in only four sittings
The National Gallery in London has preserved the work since 1862

oath-horatii.title: Oath of the Horatii
oath-horatii.description: Manifesto of Neoclassicism, exalting patriotic duty and Roman virtue.
descriptions: David painted this canvas in Rome in 1784-1785
It commemorates the oath of the three brothers before combat
The painting triumphed at the Salon of 1785
It was bought by Louis XVI for the royal collections
The Louvre has preserved the work since the Revolution

death-marat.title: The Death of Marat
death-marat.description: Revolutionary icon, the 'martyr' murdered in his bath.
descriptions: David painted this canvas in 1793, just after Marat's assassination
Marat was killed by Charlotte Corday in his bathtub on 13 July 1793
He suffered from a skin disease that forced him to work in water
The painting evokes the Italian pietàs of the Renaissance
The Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels preserve it

napoleon-crossing-alps.title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
napoleon-crossing-alps.description: Heroic equestrian portrait commissioned by Napoleon himself.
descriptions: David painted five versions of the painting between 1801 and 1805
Napoleon actually crossed the Alps on a mule
He refused to pose, saying 'no one knows if portraits look alike'
The names 'Bonaparte', 'Hannibal' and 'Karolus Magnus' are engraved on the rocks
The Malmaison Château preserves the first version

coronation-napoleon.title: The Coronation of Napoleon
coronation-napoleon.description: Immense 10-meter canvas showing Napoleon crowning Joséphine.
descriptions: David painted this monumental canvas between 1805 and 1807
It measures almost ten meters long by six tall
Napoleon had preferred to crown himself before Pope Pius VII
David depicted his own mother who was not present at the ceremony
The Louvre preserves the original work

death-socrates.title: The Death of Socrates
death-socrates.description: The philosopher serenely accepting hemlock, surrounded by his weeping disciples.
descriptions: David painted this canvas in 1787 in Paris
The painting was exhibited at the Salon of 1787
Socrates drinking hemlock evokes dignity in the face of injustice
The Metropolitan Museum in New York acquired it in 1931
The painting illustrates the ideals of the French Enlightenment

sabine-women.title: The Intervention of the Sabine Women
sabine-women.description: Women interposing themselves between their Sabine fathers and Roman husbands.
descriptions: David painted this canvas between 1796 and 1799
He painted it in prison after Robespierre's fall
The subject calls for national reconciliation after the Terror
The work was exhibited alone with a paid entry ticket
The Louvre has preserved it since 1819

grande-odalisque.title: La Grande Odalisque
grande-odalisque.description: Oriental nude famous for her back lengthened by three extra vertebrae.
descriptions: Ingres painted this canvas in 1814 in Rome
Caroline Murat, Napoleon's sister, commissioned it
The elongated back contains three extra vertebrae
The painting caused scandal for these anatomical 'errors' at the Salon of 1819
The Louvre acquired it in 1899

turkish-bath.title: The Turkish Bath
turkish-bath.description: Erotic tondo painted at 82, a summary of all of Ingres's nude studies.
descriptions: Ingres painted this canvas between 1852 and 1859, completed at age 82
The round format was chosen in 1863
Ingres revisits all his female nude studies from throughout his life
The painting belonged to Prince Napoleon-Jérôme
The Louvre acquired it in 1911

valpincon-bather.title: The Valpinçon Bather
valpincon-bather.description: A nude seen from behind of absolute formal purity, influenced by Raphael.
descriptions: Ingres painted this canvas in 1808 in Rome, at age 28
It was acquired by Édouard Valpinçon, a wealthy collector
The nude from behind draws inspiration from Raphael and ancient nudes
The turban and curtain create an Oriental framing
The Louvre acquired it in 1879

napoleon-throne.title: Napoleon I on His Imperial Throne
napoleon-throne.description: Hieratic frontal portrait inspired by Jupiter and Byzantine emperors.
descriptions: Ingres painted this portrait in 1806 at age 26
Napoleon never posed for Ingres, who drew inspiration from portraits
The portrait draws inspiration from the Olympian Zeus by Phidias
The portrait was heavily criticized by David, Ingres's former master
The Army Museum in Paris has preserved it since 1832

apotheosis-homer.title: The Apotheosis of Homer
apotheosis-homer.description: Monumental tribute to the Greek poet surrounded by the great artists of history.
descriptions: Ingres painted this canvas in 1827 for the ceiling of the Louvre
It celebrates Homer surrounded by the great writers and artists
The painting was taken down from the ceiling and hung on the walls in 1855
Ingres wanted to summarize the classical ideal in it
The Louvre preserves it in the Neoclassical section

psyche-cupid.title: Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss
psyche-cupid.description: Masterpiece of grace and tenderness, capturing the moment of awakening.
descriptions: Canova sculpted this work between 1787 and 1793
He drew inspiration from Apuleius's tale in The Golden Ass
The white marble conveys the tenderness of the moment
The sculptor worked the marble like a precious fabric
The Louvre acquired it in 1824 thanks to Joachim Murat

pauline-borghese.title: Pauline Bonaparte as Venus Victorious
pauline-borghese.description: Bold portrait of Napoleon's sister as the goddess of love.
descriptions: Canova sculpted Pauline Borghese between 1804 and 1808
Pauline was Napoleon Bonaparte's younger sister
She posed nude despite the scandal it caused
The sculpture evokes Venus Victrix holding the apple of Paris
The Borghese Gallery in Rome still preserves it

three-graces-canova.title: The Three Graces
three-graces-canova.description: Ideal of female beauty in the purest marble.
descriptions: Canova sculpted two versions of the Three Graces around 1815-1817
The first was commissioned by Joséphine de Beauharnais
Joséphine died before delivery; her son Eugène received it
It is now at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
The second was commissioned by the Duke of Bedford

portrait-mlle-riviere.title: Portrait of Mademoiselle Rivière
portrait-mlle-riviere.description: A young woman in a landscape, with the perfect oval of the face.
descriptions: Ingres painted this portrait in 1806 when he was only 26
The perfectly oval face became a stylistic signature of Ingres
Young Caroline Rivière died a few months after posing, at age 15
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting marks the rise of Neoclassicism in French portraiture

oedipus-sphinx.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
oedipus-sphinx.description: The hero solving the creature's riddle.
descriptions: Ingres painted this canvas in Rome in 1808 as a Villa Medici submission
The scene illustrates the riddle posed by the Sphinx to the Greek hero
Oedipus's athletic body betrays Ingres's admiration for ancient statuary
The painting is displayed at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Ingres revisited this subject several times throughout his career

roger-angelica.title: Roger Freeing Angelica
roger-angelica.description: A knight on a hippogriff saving the princess from the dragon.
descriptions: The painting is inspired by Ariosto's poem Orlando Furioso, written in the 16th century
Ingres painted this canvas in 1819 to decorate the Palace of Versailles
Angelica is depicted in a very stretched Mannerist pose
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Salvador Dalí drew inspiration from this composition for his own works

jupiter-thetis.title: Jupiter and Thetis
jupiter-thetis.description: The nymph pleads with the king of the gods.
descriptions: Ingres painted this monumental work in 1811 as a final Rome submission
The scene illustrates a passage from Homer's Iliad
Thetis's distorted anatomy heralds Ingres's plastic freedom
The work is preserved at the Granet Museum in Aix-en-Provence
The painting was very poorly received when presented at the Salon of 1811

comtesse-haussonville.title: Portrait of the Comtesse d'Haussonville
comtesse-haussonville.description: Elegant portrait of a pensive aristocrat.
descriptions: Ingres worked three years on this portrait before completing it in 1845
Countess Louise leans against a fireplace in a thoughtful pose
The mirror behind her reveals the nape of her neck in a subtle play of reflection
The work is part of the Frick Collection in New York
The blue silk dress is one of Ingres's bravura pieces

source-ingres.title: The Source
descriptions: Ingres began this work in 1820 but only completed it in 1856, at age 76
The painting represents the allegory of a personified water spring
The nude follows the canons of antiquity and the Italian Renaissance
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Picasso and many modernists paid tribute to this composition

princess-broglie.title: Princess Albert de Broglie
descriptions: Ingres completed this portrait in 1853 after four years of work
Princess Pauline is depicted in a brilliant blue satin dress
She died prematurely of tuberculosis six years after the portrait
The painting is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
The rendering of fabrics is considered a peak of Ingres's virtuosity

mme-moitessier-seated.title: Madame Moitessier Seated
mme-moitessier-seated.description: Portrait of a bourgeoise in a floral dress.
descriptions: Ingres took twelve years to complete this portrait, finished in 1856
The pose is inspired by a Roman fresco from Herculaneum
The chintz floral dress illustrates the wealth of the Second Empire bourgeoisie
The work is displayed at the National Gallery in London
The mirror reflection reveals Madame Moitessier's profile

antiochus-stratonice.title: Antiochus and Stratonice
antiochus-stratonice.description: The prince ill with love for his stepmother.
descriptions: Ingres painted this scene in 1840 for the Duke of Orléans
The subject comes from a story by Plutarch about the Seleucid prince
The physician Erasistratus discovers the romantic cause of the illness
The work is preserved at the Condé Museum in Chantilly
The architecture of the setting was made from sketches by Victor Baltard

portrait-bertin.title: Monsieur Bertin
portrait-bertin.description: Portrait of the newspaper director, an icon of the bourgeoisie.
descriptions: Ingres painted this portrait in 1832 of the founder of the Journal des débats
The powerful pose made it the icon of the 19th-century bourgeois
Manet reportedly said this portrait was the Buddha of the bourgeoisie
The work is displayed at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Édouard Manet considered this painting a masterpiece

paolo-francesca.title: Paolo and Francesca
paolo-francesca.description: Dante's lovers caught by the jealous husband.
descriptions: The subject is taken from Canto V of Dante's Inferno
Ingres produced several versions of this scene between 1814 and 1845
The lovers are caught reading a courtly romance
A version is preserved at the Museum of Fine Arts in Angers
The subject inspired Rodin for his sculpture The Kiss

lictors-brutus.title: The Lictors Bring to Brutus the Bodies of His Sons
lictors-brutus.description: The Roman consul sacrifices his sons for the Republic.
descriptions: David painted this painting in 1789, on the eve of the French Revolution
Brutus condemned his sons to death for conspiracy against the Republic
The contrast between the dark hero and the weeping women structures the work
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting was perceived as a Republican manifesto by contemporaries

madame-recamier.title: Portrait of Madame Récamier
madame-recamier.description: Unfinished portrait of the famous salonnière.
descriptions: David painted this portrait in 1800 but never finished it
Juliette Récamier was the queen of Parisian salons of the Directory
Her white classical dress launched a fashion throughout Europe
The work is displayed at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The bronze candelabra was designed by David himself

leonidas-thermopylae.title: Leonidas at Thermopylae
leonidas-thermopylae.description: The Spartan king before the fatal battle.
descriptions: David worked fifteen years on this canvas, completed in 1814
Leonidas and his 300 Spartans faced the Persian army in 480 BC
Napoleon did not like this painting, preferring victorious subjects
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
David painted this work during the decline of the Napoleonic Empire

mars-disarmed.title: Mars Being Disarmed by Venus
mars-disarmed.description: David's last great work in exile.
descriptions: David painted this work in exile in Brussels in 1824
The painting was his last great painting before his death in 1825
Mars is disarmed by Venus and the Graces in a cloudy palace
The work is preserved at the Royal Museums of Fine Arts in Brussels
David exhibited this painting at a successful paid exhibition

napoleon-study.title: The Emperor Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries
napoleon-study.description: The Emperor working late at night.
descriptions: David painted this portrait in 1812 commissioned by a Scottish aristocrat
Napoleon is depicted having worked all night on state affairs
The clock reads 4:13 in the morning and the candles are almost consumed
The work is preserved at the National Gallery of Art in Washington
The painting aimed to present the Emperor as a tireless worker

cupid-psyche-gerard.title: Psyche and Cupid
cupid-psyche-gerard.description: The first kiss of the mythological lovers.
descriptions: François Gérard painted this work in 1798, David's favorite student
The scene illustrates the lovers' encounter taken from Apuleius
Psyche is unaware that her lover is the god Cupid himself
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting was a great success at the Salon of 1798

madame-recamier-gerard.title: Madame Récamier
madame-recamier-gerard.description: The famous salonnière in a white dress in a landscape.
descriptions: François Gérard painted Madame Récamier in 1805
Juliette Récamier posed for many painters of her time
The pose contrasts with that of David, who had depicted her reclining
The portrait is displayed at the Carnavalet Museum in Paris
The transparent white dress illustrates the fashion of the First Empire

battle-austerlitz-gerard.title: The Battle of Austerlitz
battle-austerlitz-gerard.description: Napoleon receiving the surrender of the Austrian generals after his greatest victory.
descriptions: François Gérard painted this monumental canvas in 1810 on Napoleon's commission
The battle of 2 December 1805 is considered Napoleon's tactical masterpiece
The work measures over 10 meters long and features dozens of figures
The painting is preserved at the Palace of Versailles
The scene shows Napoleon receiving the surrender of the Austrian generals

sleep-endymion.title: The Sleep of Endymion
sleep-endymion.description: The shepherd loved by Selene bathed in moonlight.
descriptions: Girodet painted this work in 1791 at just 24 years old
Endymion was condemned by Zeus to eternal sleep out of jealousy
The bluish moonlight symbolizes the goddess Selene in love
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting marks the beginnings of French Pre-Romanticism

flood-girodet.title: Scene of a Flood
flood-girodet.description: A family trying to escape the rising waters.
descriptions: Girodet painted this dramatic scene in 1806
The painting does not depict the biblical Flood but a human catastrophe
A family tries to flee the rising waters by climbing a tree
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting won a decennial prize in 1810, beating David's Coronation

atala-tomb-girodet.title: The Entombment of Atala
atala-tomb-girodet.description: A scene from Chateaubriand — the young Christian Indian carried to the tomb.
descriptions: Girodet painted this canvas in 1808, inspired by Chateaubriand's novel
Atala is a young Christian Indian girl who died to preserve her vow of chastity
The pose of Christ on the cross is reflected in that of the deceased Atala
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting contributed to the popularity of the novel Atala throughout Europe

portrait-napoleon-gros.title: Napoleon at the Bridge of Arcole
portrait-napoleon-gros.description: The young general brandishing the flag.
descriptions: Gros painted this portrait in 1796 in Milan, a young witness of the Italian campaign
Joséphine de Beauharnais reportedly had to hold the general on her knees so he would pose
Bonaparte was then only 27 and brandished the flag at the Arcole bridge
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting is one of the first official images of the future Emperor

plague-jaffa.title: Bonaparte Visiting the Plague Victims of Jaffa
plague-jaffa.description: Napoleon touching a plague victim like a thaumaturgic king.
descriptions: Gros painted this scene in 1804 on Napoleon's commission
Bonaparte's gesture recalls that of medieval thaumaturge kings
The episode took place during the Egyptian campaign in 1799
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
The painting aimed to erase the rumor of Bonaparte poisoning his soldiers

battle-eylau.title: Napoleon on the Battlefield of Eylau
battle-eylau.description: The Emperor contemplating the dead after the battle.
descriptions: Gros painted this painting in 1808 after the competition organized by Vivant Denon
The Battle of Eylau in February 1807 caused over 40,000 deaths
Napoleon is depicted in a gesture of pity for victims of both camps
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Géricault and Delacroix drew inspiration from this canvas for their own compositions

jason-fleece.title: Jason and the Golden Fleece
jason-fleece.description: The Greek hero holding his conquest.
descriptions: Thorvaldsen sculpted this work in 1803 in Rome and it launched his career
Jason led the Argonauts in the quest for the Golden Fleece in Colchis
The pose is directly inspired by Polykleitos's Doryphoros
The work is preserved at the Thorvaldsen Museum in Copenhagen
This statue made Thorvaldsen famous throughout Neoclassical Europe

christ-thorvaldsen.title: Christ
christ-thorvaldsen.description: Monumental statue of Christ with open arms.
descriptions: Thorvaldsen sculpted this monumental work between 1821 and 1828
Christ welcomes the faithful with open arms as a sign of universal love
The gesture is engraved in the marble: Come to me
The work is preserved at the Church of Our Lady in Copenhagen
This statue inspired the Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro

lion-lucerne.title: The Lion of Lucerne
lion-lucerne.description: Dying lion carved into the rock, a memorial to the Swiss Guards who fell in 1792.
descriptions: Thorvaldsen designed this sculpture in 1820, carved into a cliff
The monument honors the 760 Swiss Guards who fell at the Tuileries in 1792
Mark Twain called this dying lion the most moving sculpture in the world
The work is located in Lucerne, Switzerland
The lion rests on broken weapons symbolizing fidelity unto death

city.title: The City
city.description: Fragmented and colorful vision of the modern metropolis.
descriptions: Léger painted this monumental canvas in 1919 after World War I
The work fragments urban modernity into bright colored planes
The painting measures over 2 meters tall and 3 meters wide
It is preserved at the Philadelphia Museum of Art
Léger was deeply marked by the mechanization observed during the war

constructors-leger.title: The Constructors
constructors-leger.description: Workers on a metal structure, a tribute to labor and modernity.
descriptions: Léger painted this series between 1950 and 1955 as a tribute to workers
The workers are depicted on the beams of a metal structure
Léger wanted his works to be understood by the working class
The work is preserved at the National Fernand Léger Museum in Biot
The painting exalts the dignity of manual labor in the post-war period

card-game-leger.title: The Card Game
card-game-leger.description: Soldiers playing cards, tubular and mechanical forms born of the war experience.
descriptions: Léger painted this work in 1917 during his convalescence after the front
The soldiers are transformed into tubular and mechanical figures
The experience of war transformed Léger's Cubist style
The work is preserved at the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo, Netherlands
It is the first major work painted after his demobilization

portrait-picasso-gris.title: Portrait of Pablo Picasso
portrait-picasso-gris.description: Cubist tribute to the master by his Spanish disciple.
descriptions: Juan Gris painted this Cubist portrait in 1912 in Paris
The work pays homage to Picasso, neighbor and master at the Bateau-Lavoir
Gris breaks down the face into rigorous geometric facets
The painting is displayed at the Art Institute of Chicago
Picasso recognized Gris as one of the most rigorous Cubists

still-life-checked-tablecloth.title: Still Life with Checked Tablecloth
still-life-checked-tablecloth.description: Synthetic Cubist composition with bottle, glass, and newspaper.
descriptions: Juan Gris painted this work in 1915 in Paris
The still life combines bottle, glass, newspaper and checkered tablecloth
Gris practiced Synthetic Cubism with mathematical rigor
The painting is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
Gris was nicknamed the demon of logic by his contemporaries

breakfast-gris.title: The Breakfast
breakfast-gris.description: Collage and gouache, synthetic Cubism at its height.
descriptions: Juan Gris produced this work in 1914 in cut paper and gouache
The work combines pieces of wallpaper imitating wood
Gris reaches the peak of his Synthetic Cubism here
The painting is preserved at MoMA in New York
Gris died young in 1927 at just 40 years old

the-scream.title: The Scream
the-scream.description: Anguished figure on a bridge, a universal expression of modern anxiety.
descriptions: Munch painted this canvas in 1893 inspired by a walk at sunset
The artist recounted hearing an infinite scream from nature at that moment
Four versions exist, including one stolen and recovered in 2006
The original work is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
A pastel version sold for 119 million dollars in 2012

madonna-munch.title: Madonna
madonna-munch.description: Erotic representation of the Virgin as a femme fatale.
descriptions: Munch painted this provocative Madonna between 1894 and 1895
The work reinvents the Virgin as an erotic femme fatale
Munch produced five painted versions and numerous lithographs
A version is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
The scandal made Munch's international reputation

vampire-munch.title: The Vampire
vampire-munch.description: A woman kissing a man's neck, a metaphor for destructive love.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1895 as part of his Frieze of Life
The original title was Love and Pain, more subtle than Vampire
The red-haired woman seems to bite the man's neck
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
A version painted in 1894 sold for 38 million dollars in 2008

puberty.title: Puberty
puberty.description: Nude young girl with an anxious gaze, a threatening shadow behind her.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1894 in Berlin
The threatening shadow is interpreted as the fear of nascent sexuality
The nude adolescent tries to cover her body with her crossed arms
The work is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
Munch lost his mother and sister when he was very young, which weighed on his relationship with women

sick-child.title: The Sick Child
sick-child.description: Memory of the death of his sister Sophie, painted with a reduced palette.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1885-1886, at age 22
The painting evokes the death of his sister Sophie taken by tuberculosis at age 15
Munch painted six versions of this subject throughout his life
A version is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
The work was booed by Norwegian critics at its first presentation

the-kiss-klimt.title: The Kiss
the-kiss-klimt.description: Couple embracing in a field of flowers, covered in gold and decorative motifs.
descriptions: Klimt painted The Kiss between 1907 and 1908 during his golden period
The real gold used evokes the Byzantine mosaics of Ravenna
The couple floats in an abstract space at the edge of a flowering precipice
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
The painting was bought by the Austrian State as soon as it was completed

portrait-adele.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
portrait-adele.description: Woman in a golden dress adorned with geometric patterns, on a sumptuous gold background.
descriptions: Klimt painted this portrait between 1903 and 1907 in Vienna
Adele Bloch-Bauer was Klimt's muse, whom he painted twice
The painting was stolen by the Nazis and returned to Adele's niece in 2006
The work is preserved at the Neue Galerie in New York
Its sale to Ronald Lauder broke the world record in 2006

danae-klimt.title: Danaë
danae-klimt.description: Zeus visiting Danaë as a shower of gold, sensual eroticism.
descriptions: Klimt painted Danaë in 1907-1908 during his golden period
Zeus visits the imprisoned princess in the form of golden rain
The vertical format follows the form of the curled-up body
The work is preserved in a private collection in Vienna
Klimt uses real gold leaf in the divine rain

tree-of-life-klimt.title: The Tree of Life
tree-of-life-klimt.description: Monumental mosaic for the Stoclet Palace in Brussels.
descriptions: Klimt designed this frieze between 1905 and 1911 for the Stoclet Palace in Brussels
The curls of the branches form a characteristic Art Nouveau motif
The tree is framed by Expectation and Fulfillment
The cartoons are preserved at the MAK (Museum of Applied Arts) in Vienna
The Stoclet Palace is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site

judith-klimt.title: Judith I
judith-klimt.description: The biblical heroine depicted as a fin-de-siècle femme fatale.
descriptions: Klimt painted this Judith in 1901 in his first version
The biblical heroine holds the head of Holofernes with half-closed eyes
The ecstatic face shocked as much as it fascinated contemporaries
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
The model is said to be Adele Bloch-Bauer, Klimt's favorite patron

embrace-schiele.title: The Embrace
embrace-schiele.description: Couple embracing in a white sheet — emotional intensity.
descriptions: Schiele painted this work in 1917, shortly before his premature death
The couple is said to represent the artist with his wife Edith
The crumpled white sheet contrasts with the flesh of the entwined lovers
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
Schiele died the following year at 28 from the Spanish flu

death-maiden-schiele.title: Death and the Maiden
death-maiden-schiele.description: Self-portrait with his mistress Wally, a premonition of their separation.
descriptions: Schiele painted this work in 1915 during his break-up with Wally Neuzil
The self-portrait depicts the artist as the figure of Death
Wally was his companion and muse for four years
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
Schiele left Wally to marry the bourgeois Edith Harms

composition-viii.title: Composition VIII
composition-viii.description: Abstract geometry influenced by the Bauhaus.
descriptions: Kandinsky painted this work in 1923 while teaching at the Bauhaus
The painting is pure geometry of circles, triangles and lines
The work marks Kandinsky's evolution toward geometric abstraction
It is preserved at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York
Kandinsky considered this canvas a synthesis of his research

yellow-red-blue.title: Yellow-Red-Blue
yellow-red-blue.description: Interaction of primary colors according to Kandinsky's theories.
descriptions: Kandinsky painted this work in 1925 at the Bauhaus in Dessau
The painting illustrates his theories on the psychology of primary colors
He wrote Concerning the Spiritual in Art in 1911 to theorize this research
The work is preserved at the National Museum of Modern Art in Paris
For Kandinsky, yellow is earthly and blue spiritual

portrait-emilie-floge.title: Portrait of Emilie Flöge
portrait-emilie-floge.description: Klimt's companion in an Art Nouveau dress.
descriptions: Klimt painted his companion Emilie Flöge in 1902 in a patterned dress
Emilie was a stylist and Klimt's intimate companion for 27 years
Klimt himself designed the Art Nouveau dresses worn by Emilie
The portrait is preserved at the Wien Museum in Vienna
Klimt never married Emilie but called her to his bedside before dying

hope-i.title: Hope I
hope-i.description: Pregnant nude woman in profile, surrounded by dark figures and decorative motifs.
descriptions: Klimt painted this work in 1903 depicting a nude pregnant woman
The subject caused a scandal upon its presentation
The model was Herma, a redhead often painted by Klimt
The work is preserved at the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa
Skulls and anguishing figures surround the mother

hope-ii.title: Hope II
hope-ii.description: Pregnant woman in a golden dress, head bowed in a richly ornamented setting.
descriptions: Klimt painted this second version in 1907-1908
The pregnant woman lowers her head toward her round belly
Three female figures in prayer surround the bottom of the composition
The work is preserved at MoMA in New York
This version is more ornamental and peaceful than the first

judith-ii.title: Judith II (Salome)
judith-ii.description: Femme fatale holding a severed head.
descriptions: Klimt painted this second Judith in 1909, sometimes called Salome
The work is more angular and expressionist than the first version
Hands outstretched like claws hold the head of Holofernes
The painting is preserved at the Galleria d'Arte Moderna in Venice
Klimt evolves here toward a more tormented and less ornamental style

death-life-klimt.title: Death and Life
death-life-klimt.description: Death observes a group of the living, entwined.
descriptions: Klimt painted this work between 1908 and 1915 in several stages
Grinning Death observes a group of living people entwined and asleep
The work received first prize at the International Exhibition in Rome in 1911
It is preserved at the Leopold Museum in Vienna
Klimt replaced the original gold background with a green-blue one after 1911

water-serpents.title: Water Serpents I
water-serpents.description: Female bodies entwined in an aquatic world.
descriptions: Klimt painted this work between 1904 and 1907 on parchment
The entwined female bodies evoke a sensual aquatic world
Gold and silver cover much of the composition
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
The painting was classified as erotic at the time, shocking critics

woman-fan.title: Lady with a Fan
woman-fan.description: Elegant woman holding a fan, colourful background with oriental patterns.
descriptions: Klimt painted this work in 1917-1918, shortly before his death
The painting integrates Japanese-inspired motifs typical of his late career
The fan traditionally symbolizes feminine seduction
The work sold for 108 million dollars in 2023, an absolute record for Klimt
The painting was the last work on Klimt's easel at his death

farm-garden.title: Farm Garden with Sunflowers
farm-garden.description: Lush garden without a horizon line.
descriptions: Klimt painted this lush garden around 1907 in the Salzkammergut
The work is part of a series of landscapes created during the summers
Klimt eliminates the horizon line to create a mosaic of flowers
The painting is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
Klimt painted his landscapes almost exclusively in square format

attersee.title: Attersee
attersee.description: The Austrian lake with pointillist reflections.
descriptions: Klimt regularly painted on the shore of Lake Attersee where he spent summers
The work dates from 1900 and adopts an almost pointillist technique
The square format accentuates the effect of a flat surface without sky
The painting is preserved at the Leopold Museum in Vienna
Klimt saw in the lake a perfect mirror for his experiments

virgin-klimt.title: The Virgin
virgin-klimt.description: Group of sleeping women with floral motifs.
descriptions: Klimt painted this work in 1913 in his late ornamental style
Seven young women are tangled in a whirlwind of patterns
The painting illustrates sexual awakening and feminine sensuality
The work is preserved at the Národní galerie in Prague
The floral motifs contrast with the white bodies of the women

fritza-riedler.title: Portrait of Fritza Riedler
fritza-riedler.description: Portrait with geometric patterns on the armchair.
descriptions: Klimt painted this portrait in 1906 during his golden period
The geometric-patterned armchair evokes a medieval halo
Fritza was the wife of a wealthy Viennese industrialist
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
The crown-shaped headdress draws inspiration from Velázquez's Las Meninas

anxiety-munch.title: Anxiety
anxiety-munch.description: Crowd with ashen faces walking on a bridge under a blood-red sky.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1894, a variant of The Scream from the previous year
The dark crowd on the bridge replaces the lone figure of The Scream
The work is part of the Frieze of Life, Munch's major cycle
The painting is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
Munch revisited his motifs in several versions throughout his life

dance-life.title: The Dance of Life
dance-life.description: Allegory of love and the stages of female life.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1899-1900 in Åsgårdstrand, Norway
Three women embody the ages of life: young, in love and aging
The painting is part of the Frieze of Life
The work is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
The lunar column reflected in the water is a recurring motif in Munch's work

melancholy-munch.title: Melancholy
melancholy-munch.description: Man by the sea, pensive and somber.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1891 in Åsgårdstrand
The pensive man is inspired by his friend Jappe Nilssen with a broken heart
Munch produced several versions of this motif between 1891 and 1896
The painting is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
The curved shore and dark colors convey inner torment

summer-night-inger.title: Summer Night, Inger on the Beach
summer-night-inger.description: His sister seated facing the sea at dusk.
descriptions: Munch painted his sister Inger in 1889 on the beach at Åsgårdstrand
The work marks Munch's shift toward a freer brushwork
Inger was a regular model for her artist brother
The painting is preserved at the Rasmus Meyers Samlinger in Bergen
The Nordic twilight bathes the scene in an unreal light

girls-pier.title: The Girls on the Bridge
girls-pier.description: Three women on a village bridge.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1901 in Åsgårdstrand
Three young women look at the water from a white bridge
Munch painted this motif more than twelve times between 1899 and 1904
The painting is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
The yellow house and the moon are recurring elements of the motif

workers-snow.title: Workers in the Snow
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1913 in Ekely near Oslo
The painting marks Munch's late interest in the working world
Tired workers return through the snow after their day
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
Munch moves away here from existential anguish toward social realism

jealousy-munch.title: Jealousy
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1895 as part of the Frieze of Life
The jealous man observes a couple inspired by Adam and Eve
The haggard face occupies the entire foreground in close-up
The painting is preserved at the Rasmus Meyers Samlinger in Bergen
Munch drew inspiration from his painful friendship with Stanisław Przybyszewski

red-virginia-creeper.title: Red Virginia Creeper
red-virginia-creeper.description: House overrun by a blood-red plant.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1898-1900
The blood-red Virginia creeper evokes passion or crime
A tragic silhouette in the foreground stares at the viewer
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
The painting is among the artist's most anguishing works

self-portrait-clock.title: Self-Portrait between the Clock and the Bed
self-portrait-clock.description: Munch standing between a clock and a bed, a gaunt figure in a colourful interior.
descriptions: Munch painted this self-portrait between 1940 and 1943 toward the end of his life
The clock without hands symbolizes time slipping from the artist
The bed represents the final rest that is approaching
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
Munch died in 1944 at Ekely, shortly after this meditation on death

ashes-munch.title: Ashes
ashes-munch.description: A couple after lovemaking, despair and regret.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1895 as part of the Frieze of Life
The woman holds her temples facing a prostrate man
The work shows the disillusion that follows romantic passion
The painting is preserved at the Nasjonalgalleriet in Oslo
Munch paints here the opposite of desire: the awareness of its end

separation.title: Separation
separation.description: A man abandoning a weeping woman.
descriptions: Munch painted this work in 1896 during a stay in Paris
The blonde woman moves away while the man holds his heart
The woman's long hair transforms into a climbing plant
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
Munch paints absence here as physical pain

consolation.title: Consolation
descriptions: Munch painted this work around 1894 in his Frieze of Life
A nude couple comforts each other in shared distress
The painting evokes the torments of romantic relationships
The work is preserved at the Munch Museum in Oslo
Munch never wanted to marry despite several passionate relationships

family-schiele.title: The Family
family-schiele.description: Unfinished work, the last painting before his death.
descriptions: Schiele painted this work in 1918, shortly before his death
The painting depicts the artist, his wife Edith and an unborn child
Edith died pregnant from the Spanish flu in October 1918
The work is preserved at the Österreichische Galerie Belvedere in Vienna
Schiele died three days after Edith, at just 28 years old

cardinal-nun.title: Cardinal and Nun
cardinal-nun.description: Religious couple embracing, scandalous for its time.
descriptions: Schiele painted this provocative work in 1912
The religious couple parodies The Kiss by Klimt, his master
Schiele was imprisoned shortly after for drawings deemed obscene
The work is preserved at the Leopold Museum in Vienna
Schiele sought to shock puritan Viennese society

autumn-trees.title: Autumn Trees
autumn-trees.description: Bare trees in an expressionist landscape.
descriptions: Schiele painted several landscapes of trees between 1910 and 1916
The tortured branches evoke human anguish
Schiele projected his state of mind onto nature
The work is preserved at the Leopold Museum in Vienna
The skeletal trees are characteristic of the Expressionist style

reclining-nude-modigliani.title: Reclining Nude
reclining-nude-modigliani.description: Sensual nude with direct gaze, a scandal at its exhibition.
descriptions: Modigliani painted several reclining nudes between 1916 and 1919
A version sold for 170 million dollars in 2015, one of the most expensive in the world
The exhibition of these nudes in 1917 was closed by police for indecency
Dealer Léopold Zborowski commissioned this series of nudes
Modigliani drew inspiration from Renaissance Venuses in modern poses

jeanne-hebuterne.title: Portrait of Jeanne Hébuterne
jeanne-hebuterne.description: His companion and muse with the characteristic elongated neck.
descriptions: Modigliani painted several portraits of his companion Jeanne between 1917 and 1919
Jeanne was 14 years younger than the artist and studied art in Paris
The elongated neck and pupilless eyes characterize his style
A version is displayed at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
Jeanne committed suicide while pregnant the day after Modigliani's death in 1920

lunia-czechowska.title: Portrait of Lunia Czechowska
lunia-czechowska.description: Oval face with almond-shaped eyes without pupils.
descriptions: Modigliani painted several portraits of Lunia Czechowska between 1917 and 1919
Lunia was the Polish friend of dealer Zborowski
The almond-shaped eyes without pupils evoke African masks
A version is at the Modern Art Museum of the City of Paris
Lunia later described Modigliani as a rare and sensitive man

cellist-modigliani.title: The Cellist
cellist-modigliani.description: Musician playing the cello in dark tones and angular shapes.
descriptions: Modigliani painted this work in 1909 in Paris
The painting dates from the period preceding his mature style
Cézanne's influence is still visible in the treatment of volumes
The painting was presented at the Salon des Indépendants in 1910
This work marks the transition to his characteristic elongated style

alice-modigliani.title: Alice
alice-modigliani.description: Portrait of a child with a melancholy gaze.
descriptions: Modigliani painted this child portrait in 1918 in the South of France
The melancholy child is part of a series of child portraits
Modigliani had taken refuge in Nice during the war
The work is preserved at the Statens Museum for Kunst in Copenhagen
The empty eyes give the model a troubling presence

bride-groom.title: The Bride and Groom
bride-groom.description: Double portrait with elongated and stylized forms.
descriptions: Modigliani painted this double portrait in 1915-1916
The stylized couple may be inspired by a wedding observed in Paris
The elongated forms characterize the artist's mature style
The work is preserved at MoMA in New York
Modigliani was influenced by African masks and archaic sculpture

departure-beckmann.title: Departure
departure-beckmann.description: Allegorical triptych on the flight from Nazi Germany.
descriptions: Beckmann painted this triptych between 1932 and 1935 in Germany
The work symbolizes flight in the face of the rise of Nazism
Beckmann exiled himself from Germany in 1937, the day the Degenerate Art exhibition opened
The triptych is preserved at MoMA in New York
The side panels show tortures while the center offers liberation

self-portrait-tuxedo.title: Self-Portrait in Tuxedo
self-portrait-tuxedo.description: The artist as a melancholy dandy.
descriptions: Beckmann painted this self-portrait in 1927
The artist depicts himself as a dandy at the peak of his career
Beckmann produced dozens of self-portraits throughout his life
The work is preserved at the Busch-Reisinger Museum in Cambridge, Massachusetts
The painting expresses both social success and melancholy

night-beckmann.title: The Night
night-beckmann.description: A chaotic scene of domestic violence, the trauma of the postwar period.
descriptions: Beckmann painted this traumatic work in 1918-1919
The scene evokes the collapse of Germany after the Great War
Three torturers torment a family in a narrow room
The work is preserved at the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen in Düsseldorf
Beckmann had served as a medic at the front and was deeply marked

street-berlin.title: Street Scene in Berlin
street-berlin.description: Elegant women in the modern metropolis.
descriptions: Kirchner painted several Berlin street scenes between 1913 and 1915
The depicted women are often elegant prostitutes
The angular forms convey the agitation of the modern metropolis
A version is preserved at the Neue Galerie in New York
Kirchner painted these scenes shortly before World War I

self-portrait-soldier.title: Self-Portrait as a Soldier
self-portrait-soldier.description: The artist traumatized by the war.
descriptions: Kirchner painted this self-portrait in 1915 in Halle
The artist depicts himself with his right hand severed, symbolically
Kirchner had been declared unfit for service due to psychological collapse
The work is preserved at the Allen Memorial Art Museum in Oberlin
The nude female model in the background contrasts with the soldier's distress

five-women-street.title: Five Women on the Street
five-women-street.description: Elegant women with angular forms on a Berlin street.
descriptions: Kirchner painted this work in 1913 in Berlin
The elegant women in fur collars are stylized like marionettes
The painting captures the alienation of modern urban life
The work is preserved at the Museum Ludwig in Cologne
Kirchner founded the Expressionist group Die Brücke in 1905

composition-vii.title: Composition VII
composition-vii.description: Considered the pinnacle of Kandinsky's abstract work.
descriptions: Kandinsky painted this monumental work in 1913 in Munich
The painting evokes the themes of the Flood, Last Judgment and Resurrection
Kandinsky considered it the culmination of his Compositions
The work is preserved at the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow
The artist produced over 30 preparatory studies before painting the final canvas

first-abstract-watercolor.title: First Abstract Watercolor
first-abstract-watercolor.description: Possibly the first abstract work in history.
descriptions: Kandinsky dated this work 1910 to make it the first abstract work
The date has been contested and would rather be 1913
The watercolor marks the definitive break with figuration
It is preserved at the Centre Pompidou in Paris
Kandinsky sought in abstraction the visual equivalent of music

blue-rider.title: The Blue Rider
descriptions: Kandinsky painted this work in 1903, still figurative
The rider symbolizes the artistic movement of the same name founded in 1911
Blue was for Kandinsky the spiritual color par excellence
The work is preserved in the E.G. Bührle Collection in Zurich
The Blue Rider brought together Kandinsky, Marc, Macke and Klee

improvisation-28.title: Improvisation 28
improvisation-28.description: A play of spontaneous shapes and colors.
descriptions: Kandinsky painted this work in 1912 in Munich
The artist classified his works into Impressions, Improvisations and Compositions
The Improvisations arose spontaneously from the unconscious according to Kandinsky
The work is preserved at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York
Kandinsky wrote Concerning the Spiritual in Art in 1911 to theorize his approach

thinker.title: The Thinker
thinker.description: Meditative figure originally conceived to crown The Gates of Hell.
descriptions: Rodin conceived The Thinker in 1880 for The Gates of Hell
The figure originally represented Dante meditating on Hell
An enlargement in 1904 made The Thinker a universal figure
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Over 28 monumental bronzes exist throughout the world

kiss-rodin.title: The Kiss
kiss-rodin.description: Paolo and Francesca from the Divine Comedy embracing for eternity.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted The Kiss between 1882 and 1889 for The Gates of Hell
The subject is taken from Canto V of Dante's Inferno: Paolo and Francesca
Rodin removed the group from the Gates because it seemed too happy there
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The work's sensuality caused scandal upon its presentation

burghers-calais.title: The Burghers of Calais
burghers-calais.description: Monument to the six hostages who sacrificed themselves to save their town.
descriptions: Rodin received the commission for this monument in 1885 from the city of Calais
The six burghers surrendered to the English king in 1347 to save their city
Rodin refused to hierarchize the figures, scandalizing the commissioner
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Twelve original casts exist throughout the world

age-of-bronze.title: The Age of Bronze
age-of-bronze.description: So realistic that Rodin was accused of having cast a living body.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted this work in 1875-1877 during a trip to Italy
The realism was such that Rodin was accused of casting from life
The model was a Belgian soldier named Auguste Neyt
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The accusation was dropped after an official inquiry proved Rodin's talent

balzac-rodin.title: Monument to Balzac
balzac-rodin.description: Massive silhouette of the writer in a dressing gown.
descriptions: Rodin worked seven years on this commission from the Société des gens de lettres
The final model was rejected in 1898 and called a colossal sketch
Rodin kept the plaster at home and the bronze was only erected in 1939
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The monument now stands on Boulevard Raspail in Paris

eve-rodin.title: Eve
eve-rodin.description: The first woman covering her body in shame.
descriptions: Rodin conceived Eve between 1881 and 1899 for The Gates of Hell
The model was pregnant without telling Rodin during the sessions
Rodin noticed the changes in the body and found the work more human
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Eve covers her face in shame after the biblical fall

adam-rodin.title: Adam
adam-rodin.description: Tormented male figure pointing to the ground.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted Adam in 1880 as a counterpart to his Eve
The pose is inspired by Michelangelo's dead Christ in the Pietà
The finger pointing to the ground evokes the creation by God
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Rodin passionately admired Michelangelo, discovered during his Italian trip

three-shades.title: The Three Shades
three-shades.description: Three identical figures atop The Gates of Hell.
descriptions: Rodin conceived the Three Shades to crown The Gates of Hell
The three figures are identical but placed in a circle
The gesture points to the inscription You who enter, abandon all hope
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Rodin often reused the same figure in several compositions

ugolino-rodin.title: Ugolino
ugolino-rodin.description: The count devouring his children, after Dante.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted Ugolino in 1882 based on Dante's episode
The Count of Pisa was imprisoned with his sons and died of hunger
The bronze shows Ugolino crawling over the bodies of his children
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The subject also inspired Carpeaux but Rodin chose a more brutal treatment

prodigal-son-rodin.title: The Prodigal Son
descriptions: Rodin conceived this isolated figure from a group of The Gates of Hell
The work expresses the repentance and imploring of the repentant son
Rodin sculpted this figure starting in the 1880s
The bronze is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The desperate gesture is inspired by late Baroque

eternal-springtime.title: Eternal Springtime
eternal-springtime.description: A couple embracing in amorous ecstasy.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted this work in 1884 as a gift for his friend Robert Louis Stevenson
The couple was originally intended for The Gates of Hell
The work celebrates the romantic encounter of Rodin and Camille Claudel
A version is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The cheerfulness of this work contrasts with the suffering of the Gates

walking-man-rodin.title: The Walking Man
walking-man-rodin.description: Torso and legs without arms or head — pure dynamics.
descriptions: Rodin conceived this figure between 1899 and 1907 without head or arms
The work combines a torso from 1878 and legs added later
The fragment alone expresses, according to Rodin, the essence of movement
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Rodin defended the idea that incomplete sculpture was more expressive

danaid-rodin.title: The Danaid
danaid-rodin.description: A woman collapsed on her jar, eternal damnation.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted this work in 1885 based on the Greek myth
The Danaids were condemned to eternally fill a leaking barrel
The model was reportedly Camille Claudel according to several historians
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
The curved back expresses exhaustion and eternal damnation

i-am-beautiful.title: I Am Beautiful
i-am-beautiful.description: A man lifting a woman, after Baudelaire.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted this work in 1882 based on a poem by Baudelaire
The title comes from Les Fleurs du mal: I am beautiful, O mortals, as a dream of stone
The man lifts the woman in a gesture of tragic adoration
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Rodin combined here two pre-existing figures from The Gates of Hell

cathedral-hands.title: The Cathedral
cathedral-hands.description: Two right hands joined, forming an arch.
descriptions: Rodin sculpted this work in 1908 in plaster then in stone
The work is formed of two right hands from different people
The fingers form an arch evoking Gothic vaults
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Rodin said that hands had their own language

pierre-wissant.title: Pierre de Wissant
pierre-wissant.description: One of the Burghers of Calais, in a dramatic pose.
descriptions: Pierre de Wissant is one of the six Burghers of Calais sculpted by Rodin
His dramatic pose expresses doubt in the face of imminent sacrifice
Rodin sculpted each figure so it could be presented in isolation
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
