The Burghers offered themselves barefoot with ropes around their necks to the English king in 1347

jean-aire.title: Jean d'Aire
jean-aire.description: Burgher of Calais carrying the key to the city.
descriptions: Jean d'Aire is the most determined of the six Burghers of Calais
He carries the key of the city which he symbolically delivers to the English king
Rodin sculpted this figure in isolation at several scales
The work is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
His upright posture contrasts with the despair of other burghers in the group

waltz-claudel.title: The Waltz
waltz-claudel.description: A couple embraced in a whirling dance movement.
descriptions: Camille Claudel sculpted The Waltz in 1893 in Paris
The erotic subject of the entwined couple caused a scandal
The work was refused for public commission as too sensual
A version is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Claudel had to add drapery to the final version to make it public

maturity-claudel.title: The Age of Maturity
maturity-claudel.description: Allegory of the breakup with Rodin.
descriptions: Camille Claudel sculpted this allegory between 1893 and 1903
The work symbolizes Claudel's abandonment by Rodin for Rose Beuret
The young kneeling woman reaches her arms toward the man drawn away by old age
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Rodin tried to block the public commission of this work, considering it too personal

sakountala.title: Sakountala
sakountala.description: A couple from Indian mythology embracing.
descriptions: Camille Claudel sculpted this work in 1888 inspired by an Indian legend
The couple represents Sakountala finding her husband again after a long separation
The work was acclaimed at the Salon des artistes français of 1888
A version is preserved at the Rodin Museum in Paris
Claudel was wrongly accused of having copied Rodin's Eternal Springtime

dance-carpeaux.title: The Dance
dance-carpeaux.description: Exuberant group for the Palais Garnier.
descriptions: Carpeaux sculpted this group in 1869 for the facade of the Opéra Garnier
The sensuality of the figures caused a public scandal
An inkwell was thrown at the work by a protester in 1869
The original is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
A cast replaced the original on the facade of the Opera

ugolino-carpeaux.title: Ugolino and His Sons
ugolino-carpeaux.description: The count from the Divine Comedy dying of hunger.
descriptions: Carpeaux sculpted Ugolino during his stay in Rome in 1860-1862
The subject is taken from Canto XXXIII of Dante's Inferno
The Count of Pisa gnaws his fingers in despair before his dying children
A version is displayed at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
The work exalts Romantic pathos and anatomical mastery

quatre-parties-monde.title: The Four Parts of the World
quatre-parties-monde.description: Figures representing the continents holding a globe.
descriptions: Carpeaux sculpted this fountain in 1872 for the Observatory garden in Paris
The four continents together carry the terrestrial sphere
Africa is depicted breaking its chains, a tribute to the abolition of slavery
A version is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Carpeaux died in 1875 shortly after the fountain's completion

mediterranean-maillol.title: The Mediterranean
mediterranean-maillol.description: A seated woman with full, serene forms.
descriptions: Maillol sculpted this work between 1902 and 1905
The seated figure expresses Mediterranean serenity
Maillol abandoned tapestry for sculpture around age 40
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
André Gide wrote that the work was beautiful because it meant nothing

river-maillol.title: The River
river-maillol.description: A reclining female figure symbolizing water.
descriptions: Maillol sculpted this monumental work between 1938 and 1943
The work was commissioned in memory of pacifist writer Henri Barbusse
The reversed female figure evokes flowing waters
The work is preserved at MoMA in New York
Maillol died in 1944 in a car accident before the definitive erection

pomona-maillol.title: Pomona
pomona-maillol.description: Goddess of fruit with generous forms.
descriptions: Maillol sculpted Pomona around 1910 inspired by the Roman goddess of fruits
The figure holds fruit in her outstretched hands
The work has stood in the Tuileries garden in Paris since 1964
Minister André Malraux had several Maillol works installed in the Tuileries
Maillol revolutionized sculpture by returning to full and serene forms

hercules-archer.title: Hercules the Archer
hercules-archer.description: The hero drawing his bow — maximum tension.
descriptions: Bourdelle sculpted Heracles the Archer in 1909 in Paris
The work depicts the sixth of the twelve labors: the Stymphalian birds
Bourdelle worked in Rodin's workshop for 15 years
The work is preserved at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris
The physical tension of the hero revolutionized modern sculpture

dying-centaur.title: Dying Centaur
descriptions: Bourdelle sculpted this work in 1914 on the eve of war
The dying centaur symbolizes the end of ancient paganism
Bourdelle wrote that the centaur died because he had lost the faith
The work is preserved at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris
The work is considered one of his allegorical masterpieces

penelope-bourdelle.title: Penelope
penelope-bourdelle.description: Ulysses's faithful wife waiting, draped and meditative.
descriptions: Bourdelle sculpted this work between 1905 and 1912
Penelope awaits the return of Ulysses for twenty years
The model was reportedly the artist's wife Cléopâtre Sevastos
The work is preserved at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris
The meditative pose refers to Penelope's conjugal fidelity

beethoven-bourdelle.title: Beethoven, Great Tragedy
beethoven-bourdelle.description: Monumental bust of the composer, tormented expression of musical genius.
descriptions: Bourdelle sculpted over 80 busts of Beethoven during his life
The composer was an obsessive figure for the artist
Bourdelle saw in Beethoven the incarnation of tragic genius
The work is preserved at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris
The sculptor said he felt Beethoven as a brother

france-bourdelle.title: France
france-bourdelle.description: Allegorical figure of the homeland, draped and warlike.
descriptions: Bourdelle sculpted La France in 1922-1925 for the centenary of American engagement
The work was erected at Pointe de Grave near Bordeaux in 1925
The helmeted figure holds a brandished sword as a sign of defense
A version is preserved at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris
The allegory of the victorious homeland honors the American soldiers of 1917

eve-despiau.title: Eve
eve-despiau.description: A classical female figure of great serenity.
descriptions: Despiau sculpted Eve in 1924-1925
The artist was Rodin's assistant for seven years
The work marks the return to a calmed classicism after the war
It is preserved at the National Museum of Modern Art in Paris
Despiau favored sobriety and psychological finesse in his portraits

discobolus.title: Discobolus
discobolus.description: An athlete frozen in the instant of throwing the discus.
descriptions: Myron sculpted this work around 460-450 BC in bronze
The Greek original is lost and only Roman marble copies survive
The athlete is frozen in the suspended moment of throwing the discus
A famous copy is preserved at the Vatican Museums
The work illustrates kalokagathia, the ideal of classical Greek art

apollo-belvedere.title: Apollo Belvedere
apollo-belvedere.description: Ideal of male beauty in antiquity.
descriptions: This statue is a Roman copy of a Greek original attributed to Leochares
It was discovered at the end of the 15th century and entered the Vatican in 1511
Winckelmann made it the absolute ideal of ancient beauty
The work is preserved at the Vatican Museums
The nickname comes from the Belvedere palace where it was installed in Rome

belvedere-torso.title: Belvedere Torso
descriptions: The Belvedere Torso dates from the 1st century BC
It is signed by Apollonios of Athens, son of Nestor
Michelangelo made it one of his major sources of inspiration
The work is preserved at the Vatican Museums
The fragment is said to represent Hercules at rest according to recent hypotheses

woman-hat-matisse.title: Woman with a Hat
woman-hat-matisse.museum: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
woman-hat-matisse.description: The 'Fauve' colors of this portrait caused a scandal at the Salon d'Automne.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1905 depicting his wife Amélie
Presented at the Salon d'Automne, it triggered the Fauvist movement
Critic Louis Vauxcelles spoke of a 'cage of wild beasts' before these canvases
The work is preserved at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
Gertrude Stein bought the scandalous painting in 1905

dance-matisse.title: Dance
dance-matisse.description: Round of red figures on a blue and green background — primitive joy.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1909-1910 for collector Sergei Shchukin
The red figures on blue and green ground evoke a primitive dance
Matisse produced two versions a year apart
The work is preserved at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
The circle dance recalls sacred dances and ancient bacchanalia

red-room.title: The Red Room (Harmony in Red)
red-room.description: Interior saturated in red where patterns and objects merge.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1908 under the original title Harmony in Blue
The artist covered the painting in red before delivery to Shchukin
The patterns of the tapestry merge with those of the tablecloth
The work is preserved at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
This canvas overturns the traditional codes of perspective

burial-ornans.title: A Burial at Ornans
burial-ornans.description: Provincial funeral scene treated with the dignity of history painting.
descriptions: Courbet painted this monumental work in 1849-1850 in his native village
The painting measures over 6 meters long for 3 meters tall
An ordinary scene is treated on the scale of history painting
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The painting marks the official birth of Realism in painting

stone-breakers.title: The Stone Breakers
stone-breakers.description: Manifesto of social realism, destroyed during World War II.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1849 in Ornans
The two stone breakers embody the harshness of workers' labor
The painting was destroyed during the bombing of Dresden in February 1945
Only photographs bear witness to this major work
Proudhon saw in this canvas the pictorial manifesto of socialism

gleaners.title: The Gleaners
gleaners.description: Dignity of peasant labor — three women gathering ears of grain after the harvest.
descriptions: Millet painted this work in 1857 on the plain of Chailly near Barbizon
Gleaning allowed the poor to collect fallen ears of grain
The painting was controversial for its dignified portrayal of the poorest
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Van Gogh later copied the work out of admiration for Millet

angelus.title: The Angelus
angelus.description: A peasant couple praying in the fields at sunset.
descriptions: Millet painted this work between 1857 and 1859 in Barbizon
The couple recites the evening Angelus at the distant sound of the bell
The painting became one of the most reproduced works of the 19th century
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Dalí was obsessed with this painting and wrote a book about it

studio-painter.title: The Painter's Studio
studio-painter.description: Real allegory of seven years of artistic life.
descriptions: Courbet painted this monumental work in 1855 for the World's Fair
The painting was rejected and Courbet built his own Realist pavilion
The work brings together the figures who marked his artistic life
It is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Baudelaire is among the artist's friends on the right of the painting

desperate-man.title: The Desperate Man
desperate-man.description: Man gripping his hair with both hands, a wild stare fixed on the viewer.
descriptions: Courbet painted this self-portrait in 1843-1845, at age 24
The work expresses the Romantic anguish of the young artist
The wide eyes and hands in the hair mark the painting
The work is preserved in a private collection
Courbet always kept this painting in his studio as an emblem

wave-courbet.title: The Wave
wave-courbet.description: Massive foaming wave breaking under a stormy sky.
descriptions: Courbet painted several versions of The Wave starting in 1869
The artist stayed in Étretat where he observed the sea during the autumn of 1869
Cézanne admired the thickness of the material in these seascapes
A version is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The work marks Courbet's evolution toward a freer brushwork

bathers-courbet.title: The Bathers
bathers-courbet.description: Two full-figured women at the edge of a stream in a wooded undergrowth.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1853 and caused a scandal at the Salon
Napoleon III reportedly struck the painting with his riding crop
The realism of the nudes contrasts with academic idealization
The work is preserved at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier
The painting was bought by patron Alfred Bruyas

young-ladies-seine.title: Young Ladies on the Banks of the Seine
young-ladies-seine.description: Two women in light dresses lying by the Seine, one dozing in the grass.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1856-1857 and caused a scandal at the Salon
The two women with free behavior were considered courtesans
The scene takes place on the banks of the Seine near Paris
The work is preserved at the Petit Palais Museum in Paris
The painting marks the modernity of painting through its contemporary subject

meeting-courbet.title: The Meeting (Bonjour, Monsieur Courbet)
meeting-courbet.description: Three men greeting each other on a sunlit country lane, Courbet hat in hand.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1854 in Montpellier
The painting depicts Courbet's arrival at his patron Alfred Bruyas's home
The artist's proud attitude before the notable shocked critics
The work is preserved at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier
The painting was nicknamed Bonjour Monsieur Courbet in mockery

wounded-man.title: The Wounded Man
wounded-man.description: Man lying against a tree, eyes closed, a bloodstain on his white shirt.
descriptions: Courbet painted this self-portrait in 1844-1854
The face represents a woman in reality retouched later
The work expresses melancholy after the break with Virginie Binet
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Analyses have revealed another portrait beneath the one we see

sleepers.title: The Sleepers
sleepers.description: Two nude women asleep in each other's arms on an unmade bed.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1866 on commission from diplomat Khalil-Bey
Khalil-Bey also commissioned The Origin of the World the same year
The painting was forbidden from public presentation for decades
The work is preserved at the Petit Palais Museum in Paris
The lesbian subject was bold for the Second Empire

source-courbet.title: The Source
source-courbet.description: Nude woman seen from behind under a trickle of water, in a rocky, wooded landscape.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1868
The nude from behind recalls Ingres's The Source
Courbet reverses the classical canon with a more fleshy and naturalistic body
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The tree and water create an intimate landscape setting

trout-courbet.title: The Trout
trout-courbet.description: Trout laid on the stone at the river's edge, the hook still in its mouth.
descriptions: Courbet painted this work in 1872 during his captivity after the Commune
The artist identifies with the fish harpooned by the State
The inscription In vinculis faciebat means painted in chains
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Courbet died in exile in Switzerland in 1877 without being able to return to France

sower-millet.title: The Sower
sower-millet.description: Peasant sowing in the evening light.
descriptions: Millet painted this work in 1850 and presented it at the Salon
The painting shocked through its dignifying of the ordinary peasant
Van Gogh copied this painting and referenced it in his letters
The work is preserved at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston
The broad gesture of the sower evokes a quasi-biblical figure

man-hoe.title: Man with a Hoe
man-hoe.description: Exhausted worker leaning on his tool.
descriptions: Millet painted this work in 1860-1862
The exhausted worker represents the degraded peasant condition
The painting was accused of socialist realism by critics
The work is preserved at the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles
Poet Edwin Markham wrote a famous poem inspired by this painting

shepherdess-flock.title: Shepherdess with Her Flock
shepherdess-flock.description: Young woman tending her sheep in the plain.
descriptions: Millet painted this work in 1864
The shepherdess knits while watching her flock of sheep
The painting was a huge success at the Salon of 1864
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The silence and dignity of the subject make it an emblem of peasant realism

spring-millet.title: Spring
spring-millet.description: Landscape after the rain with a rainbow.
descriptions: Millet painted this work in 1868-1873 in the Seasons series
The rainbow after the storm symbolizes peasant hope
Millet died in 1875 without having completed the entire series
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The painting foreshadows the atmospheric landscapes of the Impressionists

souvenir-mortefontaine.title: Souvenir of Mortefontaine
souvenir-mortefontaine.description: Dreamy landscape with trees veiled in mist.
descriptions: Corot painted this work in 1864 from his memories of the parks of Ermenonville
The painting was bought by Napoleon III at the Salon of 1864
The trees veiled in mist create a melancholy atmosphere
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Corot favored memories over plein air studies during his last years

woman-pearl.title: Woman with a Pearl
woman-pearl.description: Portrait inspired by the Mona Lisa.
descriptions: Corot painted this work around 1858-1868
The title comes from a pearl-shaped leaf on the diadem
The pose and composition echo those of the Mona Lisa
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Corot gave this particularly cherished painting to his nephew

bridge-narni.title: The Bridge at Narni
descriptions: Corot painted this work in 1827 during his first trip to Italy
The Roman bridge spans the Nera river in Umbria
The work was painted on the spot then reworked in the studio
The work is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Corot's Italian landscapes founded his reputation in Paris

interrupted-reading.title: Interrupted Reading
descriptions: Corot painted this portrait in 1870, toward the end of his life
The model poses in a thoughtful attitude, the book suspended
Corot painted numerous portraits of isolated female figures
The work is preserved at the Art Institute of Chicago
The painting is representative of intimate figures from his last years

morning-dance-nymphs.title: Dance of the Nymphs
morning-dance-nymphs.description: Mythological creatures in a wooded undergrowth.
descriptions: Corot painted this work in 1850
The nymphs dance at dawn in a misty clearing
Corot combines mythological memory and poetic naturalism
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The work marks Corot's evolution toward a more airy style

ville-avray.title: Ville-d'Avray
ville-avray.description: Ponds that Corot painted throughout his life.
descriptions: Corot painted the family pond at Ville-d'Avray starting in the 1830s
The Corot family owned a country house near Versailles
The artist painted over 50 versions of this beloved pond
A version is preserved at the Brooklyn Museum in New York
Ville-d'Avray was Corot's intimate motif for 40 years

harvest-daubigny.title: The Harvest
harvest-daubigny.description: Golden fields under a summer sky.
descriptions: Daubigny painted this work in 1851 on the Brie plain
The painting was bought by the State at the Salon of 1852
Daubigny favored plein air painting before the Impressionists
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
The artist owned a studio boat called Le Botin to paint on rivers

banks-oise.title: The Banks of the Oise
banks-oise.description: A peaceful river, a precursor of Impressionism.
descriptions: Daubigny painted numerous views of the Oise from his studio boat
The artist settled in Auvers-sur-Oise, which he made famous
Monet and Pissarro admired his landscapes foreshadowing Impressionism
A version is preserved at the Bordeaux Museum of Fine Arts
Daubigny welcomed Cézanne and Pissarro to Auvers-sur-Oise

spring-daubigny.title: Spring
spring-daubigny.description: Orchard in bloom in spring light.
descriptions: Daubigny painted this work in 1857
The orchard in bloom evokes spring renewal
The work was partially painted in the open air
The painting is preserved at the Louvre Museum in Paris
Daubigny directly influenced Van Gogh who copied his orchards

horse-fair.title: The Horse Fair
horse-fair.description: Immense canvas of the Paris fair.
descriptions: Rosa Bonheur painted this monumental work between 1852 and 1855
The painting measures 2.5 meters tall by 5 meters long
Rosa Bonheur dressed as a man to study horses at the market
The work is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
A special authorization allowed her to wear trousers in Paris

ploughing-nivernais.title: Ploughing in the Nivernais
ploughing-nivernais.description: Team of oxen in the fields.
descriptions: Rosa Bonheur painted this work in 1849, at age 27
The painting was commissioned by the State after her Salon success
The Charolais oxen are depicted with striking animal realism
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Rosa Bonheur was the first female artist to receive the Legion of Honor

monarch-herd.title: The Monarch of the Herd
monarch-herd.description: Imposing bull in a pastoral landscape, a masterful animal study.
descriptions: Rosa Bonheur painted bulls and cattle throughout her career
The artist owned her own herd at By near Fontainebleau
Her anatomical precision made her the most famous animal painter of the 19th century
The work is preserved in a private collection
Buffalo Bill visited Rosa Bonheur in her studio in 1889

third-class-carriage.title: The Third-Class Carriage
descriptions: Daumier painted this work around 1862-1864 but never finished it
The painting denounces the conditions of poor travelers on trains
Daumier was first a caricaturist famous for his lithographs
The work is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
Daumier died almost blind in 1879 in poverty

laundress-daumier.title: The Laundress
laundress-daumier.description: A woman and child climbing a quay.
descriptions: Daumier painted this work around 1863
The woman helps her child climb the steps of the quay
The painting expresses the dignity of laborious female work
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Daumier produced several versions of this moving motif

don-quixote-daumier.title: Don Quixote and Sancho Panza
descriptions: Daumier painted several versions of Don Quixote between 1850 and 1872
The artist was obsessed with the characters from Cervantes's novel
Sancho is depicted small and stout, contrasting with the skeletal hidalgo
A version is preserved at the Neue Pinakothek in Munich
Daumier identified with Don Quixote, an idealist facing brutal reality

gismonda.title: Gismonda
gismonda.description: A poster for Sarah Bernhardt that launched Mucha's career.
descriptions: Mucha designed this poster in 1894 for Sarah Bernhardt
Mucha had six days to deliver the poster for Christmas
The work caused a sensation in Paris and launched his career instantly
The original poster is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
Sarah Bernhardt signed a six-year contract with Mucha after this poster

zodiac-mucha.title: Zodiac
zodiac-mucha.description: A woman surrounded by the twelve signs of the zodiac, typical Art Nouveau style.
descriptions: Mucha designed this poster in 1896 as an advertising calendar
The work became one of the most popular Art Nouveau posters
The twelve astrological signs surround a woman with a Greek profile
The work is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
Mucha considered it one of his most successful creations

ophelia-waterhouse.title: Ophelia
ophelia-waterhouse.description: Hamlet's heroine floating among the flowers before her drowning.
descriptions: Waterhouse painted several Ophelias between 1889 and 1910
The scene is inspired by Shakespeare's Hamlet
Ophelia sings while weaving flower crowns before drowning
The work is in a private collection
The painting is part of the Victorian fascination with Ophelia

lady-shalott.title: The Lady of Shalott
lady-shalott.description: Scene from Tennyson's poem, the cursed woman on her boat.
descriptions: Waterhouse painted this work in 1888 after Tennyson's poem
The Lady of Shalott was condemned to see the world only in a mirror
She dies floating down the river to Camelot after seeing Lancelot
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
Three candles represent the life fading on the boat

ophelia-millais.title: Ophelia
ophelia-millais.description: The model Elizabeth Siddal posed in a bathtub heated by candles.
descriptions: Millais painted this work in 1851-1852, at age 22
Elizabeth Siddal posed in a bathtub heated by candles
The candles went out and Siddal contracted severe pneumonia
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
Each flower in the painting has a precise symbolic meaning

job-mucha.title: Job
job-mucha.description: Poster for cigarette paper, with a smoking woman.
descriptions: Mucha designed this poster in 1896 for Job cigarette papers
The woman with extravagant hair became a symbol of Art Nouveau
The poster became more famous than the product it advertised
The work is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
Mucha developed what was called the Mucha style through these posters

four-seasons-mucha.title: The Four Seasons
four-seasons-mucha.description: Series of decorative panels personifying the seasons.
descriptions: Mucha created this series in 1896, his first decorative ensemble
Each season is personified by a young woman in her environment
The series was published in several versions and formats
The work is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
The Four Seasons became a classic of decorative Art Nouveau

reverie-mucha.title: Reverie
reverie-mucha.description: Pensive woman in a floral setting.
descriptions: Mucha designed this work in 1897
The pensive woman represents the dream
The painting follows the aesthetic codes of Art Nouveau
The work is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
Mucha used Parisian models for his ideal figures

slav-epic.title: The Slav Epic
slav-epic.description: Monumental cycle on the history of the Slavic peoples.
descriptions: Mucha devoted 18 years to this series of 20 monumental canvases
The work was completed between 1910 and 1928
Each canvas measures up to 8 meters wide
The work is preserved at the National Gallery in Prague
Mucha considered this work his artistic testament

dance-mucha.title: The Dance
dance-mucha.description: Decorative panel from a series on the arts.
descriptions: Mucha designed this work in a series on the arts in 1898
The work is part of a set of four decorative panels
The other arts depicted are Painting, Music and Poetry
The work is preserved in a private collection
The panels became emblematic of Art Nouveau aesthetics

medee-mucha.title: Medea
medee-mucha.description: Poster for Sarah Bernhardt in the tragedy.
descriptions: Mucha designed this poster in 1898 for Sarah Bernhardt
The play was a tragedy by Catulle Mendès performed in Paris
The blood on Medea's hands evokes the murder of her children
The work is preserved at the Mucha Museum in Prague
Bernhardt wore a serpent bracelet designed by Mucha himself

madame-matisse.title: Portrait of Madame Matisse (The Green Stripe)
madame-matisse.description: Green stripe dividing the face, anti-natural colors.
descriptions: Matisse painted this portrait of his wife Amélie in 1905
The green stripe dividing the face scandalized contemporaries
The painting was made during the Fauvist revolution
The work is preserved at the Statens Museum for Kunst in Copenhagen
Matisse here liberates color from its traditional descriptive function

joy-of-life.title: The Joy of Life
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1905-1906, a manifesto of Fauvism
The work was bought by Leo and Gertrude Stein in Paris
Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon responded to this painting the following year
The work is preserved at the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia
The scene evokes a pagan Arcadia bathed in bright colors

music-matisse.title: Music
music-matisse.description: Companion to Dance, figures playing music.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1910 for Sergei Shchukin
The painting is the counterpart of The Dance, executed for the same patron
Five red figures play violin and flute on a blue-green ground
The work is preserved at the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg
The two works adorned the staircase of the Trubetskoy palace in Moscow

goldfish-matisse.title: Goldfish
goldfish-matisse.description: An aquarium on a table, Mediterranean colors.
descriptions: Matisse painted several versions of goldfish between 1911 and 1914
The aquarium fascinated the artist who observed it for hours
The Mediterranean colors of the painting evoke trips to Morocco
A version is preserved at the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts in Moscow
Matisse said: goldfish are the still life par excellence

blue-nude-1907.title: Blue Nude (Souvenir of Biskra)
blue-nude-1907.description: Nude woman reclining in a landscape of blue and green tones.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1907 in Collioure
The subtitle Souvenir of Biskra evokes his trip to Algeria
The painting caused a scandal at the Armory Show in New York in 1913
The work is preserved at the Baltimore Museum of Art
Chicago students burned a copy in protest

odalisque-red-pants.title: Odalisque with Red Trousers
odalisque-red-pants.description: A woman languid in an Oriental interior.
descriptions: Matisse painted this work in 1921-1922 in Nice
The odalisque series marks Matisse's return to a more classical figuration
The stay in Morocco in 1912-1913 fed these orientalizing visions
The work is preserved at the National Museum of Modern Art in Paris
Matisse rented an apartment in Nice specifically for these compositions

charing-cross-bridge.title: Charing Cross Bridge
descriptions: Derain painted several views of London in 1906 on commission from dealer Vollard
Vollard sent Derain to London to rival Monet's views
The Fauve colors transform the industrial metropolis into fairyland
The work is preserved at the National Gallery of Art in Washington
Derain painted some thirty London views in a few months

boats-collioure.title: Boats at Collioure
descriptions: Derain painted this work in Collioure in 1905 with Matisse
The two artists invented Fauvism during this Mediterranean summer
The pure colors vibrate under the Roussillon sun
The work is preserved at the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen in Düsseldorf
The summer of 1905 in Collioure is considered the birth of Fauvism

dance-derain.title: The Dance
descriptions: Derain painted this work in 1906, of mythological inspiration
The dancing bathers evoke ancient bacchanalia
The painting marks Derain's transition to classical subjects
The work is preserved at the Museum of Modern Art in Troyes
Derain then moved away from Fauvism toward a return to order

big-ben-derain.title: Big Ben
big-ben-derain.description: View of London with vivid brushstrokes.
descriptions: Derain painted this view of London in 1906
The painting is part of the series commissioned by Vollard
The bright brushstrokes transform the London sky into a kaleidoscope
The work is preserved in a private collection
Derain admired the London views of Turner and Monet

oedipus-sphinx-moreau.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
oedipus-sphinx-moreau.description: Mysterious face-off between man and creature.
descriptions: Moreau painted this work in 1864, which launched his career
The painting was a triumph at the Salon of 1864
Oedipus solves the riddle: what being walks on four legs in the morning?
The work is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
Moreau renewed mythological painting through his symbolism

salome-moreau.title: Salome Dancing before Herod
salome-moreau.description: The princess dancing to obtain the head of the Baptist.
descriptions: Moreau painted this work in 1876 and caused a sensation at the Salon
Joris-Karl Huysmans praised it in his novel À rebours
The painting marked the advent of Symbolism in France
The work is preserved at the Gustave Moreau Museum in Paris
Moreau bequeathed his studio to the State to make it a museum

apparition-moreau.title: The Apparition
apparition-moreau.description: Salome facing the luminous head of John the Baptist.
descriptions: Moreau painted this watercolor in 1876 as a counterpart to Salome Dancing
The floating head of John the Baptist appears to Salome alone
Huysmans described this work as a hallucinated vision
The work is preserved at the Gustave Moreau Museum in Paris
The painting influenced Klimt for his own Judiths

jupiter-semele.title: Jupiter and Semele
jupiter-semele.description: The god reveals his fatal glory to the mortal.
descriptions: Moreau painted this work between 1894 and 1895
Semele asks to see Jupiter in all his glory and dies struck by lightning
The painting is Moreau's most complex and symbolic work
The work is preserved at the Gustave Moreau Museum in Paris
Moreau includes dozens of intertwined mythological figures in it

poor-fisherman.title: The Poor Fisherman
descriptions: Puvis de Chavannes painted this work in 1881
The painting had considerable influence on Picasso and Gauguin
Picasso painted his Life as a tribute to this melancholy work
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Seurat and the Symbolists admired the hieratic simplicity of the work

hope-puvis.title: Hope
hope-puvis.description: Female figure holding a branch in a desolate landscape.
descriptions: Puvis de Chavannes painted this work in 1872 after the war of 1870
The young woman holds an olive branch in a devastated landscape
The work symbolizes France's hope after defeat
A version is preserved at the Walters Art Museum in Baltimore
Another version is at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris

sacred-grove-puvis.title: The Sacred Grove
sacred-grove-puvis.description: Allegorical figures in an idealized landscape, an inspiration for Seurat and Gauguin.
descriptions: Puvis de Chavannes painted this work in 1884
The allegorical figures personify the Muses of the arts
The work directly influenced Seurat for Bathers at Asnières
It is preserved at the Art Institute of Chicago
Gauguin admired Puvis's serenity and drew inspiration from it in Tahiti

eye-balloon.title: The Eye, Like a Strange Balloon
eye-balloon.description: Giant eye rising into the heavens.
descriptions: Redon produced this lithograph in 1882 in an album dedicated to Edgar Poe
The work is part of Redon's Black period
The eye-balloon rises in the sky toward infinity
The work is preserved at MoMA in New York
Redon created a visionary universe before switching to color in 1890

cyclops-redon.title: The Cyclops
descriptions: Redon painted this work around 1898-1900
Polyphemus observes the sleeping nymph Galatea without her knowing
The subject is taken from Ovid's Metamorphoses
The work is preserved at the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo
Redon humanizes the monster by giving him a melancholy gaze

buddha-redon.title: The Buddha
buddha-redon.description: A spiritual figure in a halo of colors.
descriptions: Redon painted this work around 1905
The painting attests to Redon's interest in spiritual Orientalism
The bright colors contrast with his earlier black works
The work is preserved at the Musée d'Orsay in Paris
Redon explored the religions of the world in his colored period

ophelia-redon.title: Ophelia among the Flowers
ophelia-redon.description: Shakespeare's heroine in a floral setting.
descriptions: Redon painted this Ophelia in pastel around 1900-1905
The work moves away from the tragic realism of the Pre-Raphaelites
Ophelia becomes an almost decorative vision among the flowers
The work is preserved at the National Gallery in London
Pastel allowed Redon effects of unreal colors

proserpine-rossetti.title: Proserpine
proserpine-rossetti.description: Jane Morris as the goddess of the underworld holding a pomegranate.
descriptions: Rossetti painted Proserpine in 1874 with Jane Morris as model
Jane was William Morris's wife and Rossetti's mistress
Proserpine is condemned to spend six months in the underworld each year
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
Rossetti produced eight versions of this subject between 1871 and 1882

beata-beatrix.title: Beata Beatrix
beata-beatrix.description: Posthumous portrait of his wife Elizabeth Siddal.
descriptions: Rossetti painted this work between 1864 and 1870
The painting is a memorial to his wife Elizabeth Siddal who died in 1862
Elizabeth is depicted as Dante's Beatrice in a mystical vision
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
The red bird holding a poppy symbolizes Elizabeth's death by laudanum

lady-lilith-rossetti.title: Lady Lilith
lady-lilith-rossetti.description: Adam's first wife according to legend, the embodiment of sensual vanity.
descriptions: Rossetti painted this work between 1866 and 1873
Lilith is Adam's first wife according to Jewish tradition
The red-haired woman contemplates her reflection, a symbol of vanity
The work is preserved at the Delaware Art Museum in Wilmington
The model was Fanny Cornforth, Rossetti's lover

hylas-nymphs.title: Hylas and the Nymphs
hylas-nymphs.description: The beautiful Argonaut lured by the nymphs into the water.
descriptions: Waterhouse painted this work in 1896
Hylas was the companion of Hercules among the Argonauts
The water nymphs lure him and drown him in their spring
The work is preserved at the Manchester Art Gallery
The work was temporarily removed in 2018 to raise a debate on nudity

echo-narcissus.title: Echo and Narcissus
echo-narcissus.description: The nymph watching the young man in love with his reflection.
descriptions: Waterhouse painted this work in 1903 after Ovid's Metamorphoses
The nymph Echo wastes away with love for Narcissus, in love with his reflection
Narcissus will transform into a flower for not being able to love himself
The work is preserved at the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool
The subject became a psychological archetype in the 20th century

awakening-conscience.title: The Awakening Conscience
awakening-conscience.description: A kept woman experiencing a moral revelation.
descriptions: Hunt painted this work in 1853-1854
The scene shows a kept woman becoming aware of her downfall
Every detail of the painting is charged with moral symbolism
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
John Ruskin defended the painting as a Pre-Raphaelite moral manifesto

light-world.title: The Light of the World
light-world.description: Christ knocking at a door overgrown with brambles.
descriptions: Hunt painted this work between 1851 and 1853
Christ knocks at the door of the human soul, covered with brambles
The door has no outer handle: it must be opened from within
The work is preserved at Keble College in Oxford
The image was reproduced in millions of copies worldwide

scapegoat-hunt.title: The Scapegoat
scapegoat-hunt.description: A solitary goat by the Dead Sea, a symbol of sacrifice.
descriptions: Hunt painted this work in 1854-1855 on the shore of the Dead Sea
The artist settled on site for months to paint from nature
The scapegoat carried the sins of the people according to Jewish tradition
The work is preserved at the Lady Lever Art Gallery in Liverpool
Hunt wanted the work to be an allegory of Christ's sacrifice

mariana-millais.title: Mariana
mariana-millais.description: The woman from Tennyson's poem waiting for her love.
descriptions: Millais painted this work in 1851 after Tennyson's poem
Mariana was abandoned by her fiancé after the loss of her dowry
She waits in a fortified house surrounded by moats
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
The painting marks the peak of the meticulous Pre-Raphaelite style

autumn-leaves.title: Autumn Leaves
descriptions: Millais painted this work in 1855-1856
The painting evokes the passage of time and the end of childhood
The young girls prepare a fire of dead leaves at dusk
The work is preserved at the Manchester Art Gallery
Millais declared he wanted to paint the most intense emotion through the simplest means

isle-dead.title: Isle of the Dead
isle-dead.description: Mysterious boat approaching a funereal island.
descriptions: Böcklin painted five versions of this work between 1880 and 1886
The boat carries a white figure toward a funereal island
Hitler owned one of the versions, which adorned his bunker
A version is preserved at the Kunstmuseum Basel
Rachmaninoff composed a symphonic poem inspired by this painting

play-waves.title: Play of the Waves
play-waves.description: Sea creatures dancing in the waves.
descriptions: Böcklin painted this work in 1883
Tritons and Nereids frolic in the waves of a rough sea
The painting blends marine mythology and naturalistic observation
The work is preserved at the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin
Böcklin created a mythological world as an alternative to official painting

war-bocklin.title: War
war-bocklin.description: Horseman of the Apocalypse riding above a field of corpses.
descriptions: Böcklin painted this work in 1896
The painting evokes the Horsemen of the Apocalypse of Saint John
The work prophesies the horrors of the century to come
It is preserved at the Kunsthaus Zürich
The painting influenced the German Expressionists of the early 20th century

sin-stuck.title: The Sin
sin-stuck.description: Femme fatale wrapped in a serpent.
descriptions: Stuck painted this work in 1893 and caused a sensation at the Munich Secession
The coiled serpent evokes biblical temptation and the Fall
The woman's direct gaze defies the viewer
The work is preserved at the Neue Pinakothek in Munich
Stuck himself framed the painting in a massive architectural frame

guardian-paradise.title: Guardian of Paradise
guardian-paradise.description: Armed angel guarding the entrance to Eden.
descriptions: Stuck painted this work in 1889
The armed angel watches over lost innocence
The work brought Stuck success at the Munich Exhibition
It is preserved at the Museum Villa Stuck in Munich
Stuck built his own villa transformed into a museum in Munich

lucifer-stuck.title: Lucifer
lucifer-stuck.description: The fallen angel with piercing eyes enthroned in the darkness.
descriptions: Stuck painted this work in 1890
Lucifer is depicted as a tormented figure with red eyes
The painting marks the Symbolist interest in demonic figures
The work is preserved at the National Gallery of Bulgaria in Sofia
Stuck taught Kandinsky and Klee at the Munich Academy

american-gothic.title: American Gothic
american-gothic.description: Farmer and his daughter in front of their house with a Gothic window.
descriptions: Grant Wood painted this iconic work in 1930 in Iowa
The models were his sister Nan and his dentist Byron McKeeby
The house with the Gothic window inspired the painting's title
The work is preserved at the Art Institute of Chicago
The painting has become the most parodied image in American art

daughters-revolution.title: Daughters of Revolution
daughters-revolution.description: Three austere women in front of the painting Washington Crossing the Delaware, a social satire.
descriptions: Grant Wood painted this work in 1932
The work is a satire of the Daughters of the American Revolution
The association had criticized Wood for commissions seen as unpatriotic
The work is preserved at the Cincinnati Art Museum
Washington Crossing the Delaware serves as an ironic background

arbor-day-wood.title: Arbor Day
arbor-day-wood.description: Schoolchildren planting a tree, rolling Iowa landscape with soft curves.
descriptions: Grant Wood painted this work in 1932 celebrating Arbor Day
The rolling landscape is characteristic of American Iowa Regionalism
The schoolchildren plant a tree in front of their rural school
The work is preserved in a private collection
Wood embodied the Regionalist movement which valued rural America

madame-x-sargent.title: Madame X
madame-x-sargent.description: Scandalous portrait of Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau in a low-cut black dress.
descriptions: Sargent painted this portrait in 1883-1884 and caused a scandal at the Salon of 1884
Virginie Gautreau was the wife of a famous French banker
The strap initially slipped off the shoulder was repainted after the scandal
The work is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
The scandal forced Sargent to leave Paris for London

carnation-lily.title: Carnation, Lily, Lily, Rose
carnation-lily.description: Two little girls lighting Chinese lanterns in a garden at dusk.
descriptions: Sargent painted this work between 1885 and 1886 in Worcestershire
The title comes from a popular Victorian song
Sargent could only paint during the few minutes of twilight
The work is preserved at the Tate Britain in London
The little girls pose lighting Japanese lanterns

daughters-boit.title: The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
daughters-boit.description: Four sisters in a Parisian interior, composition inspired by Velázquez's Las Meninas.
descriptions: Sargent painted this work in 1882 in Paris
The four daughters of Edward Boit were aged 4 to 14
The composition is directly inspired by Velázquez's Las Meninas
The work is preserved at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston
The visible Japanese vases were donated to the museum by the Boit sisters

gassed-sargent.title: Gassed
gassed-sargent.description: Soldiers blinded by mustard gas, a tragic frieze of the First World War.
descriptions: Sargent painted this monumental work in 1919
The painting measures over 6 meters long
The work depicts British soldiers blinded by mustard gas
It is preserved at the Imperial War Museum in London
Sargent was sent to the French front in 1918 as an official war painter

lady-agnew-sargent.title: Lady Agnew of Lochnaw
lady-agnew-sargent.description: Portrait of casual elegance that made Sargent famous in London.
descriptions: Sargent painted this portrait in 1892, at age 36
Lady Agnew was a recognized beauty of Scottish high society
The work caused a sensation at the Royal Academy in 1893
The painting is preserved at the Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh
The painting's success definitively launched Sargent's London career

great-wave.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
great-wave.description: Monumental wave threatening fishing boats, with Mount Fuji in the background. Icon of Japanese art.
descriptions: Hokusai created this print around 1831, at age 70
The work is part of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series
Over 8,000 original copies were reportedly printed
A version is preserved at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
The work influenced Van Gogh, Monet and Debussy who composed La Mer

red-fuji.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
red-fuji.description: Mount Fuji glowing red under a blue sky with lenticular clouds.
descriptions: Hokusai created this print around 1831 in the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
Fuji glows red at sunrise on a summer morning
The Japanese title evokes the fresh wind and clear sky
The work exists in many copies from the Edo period
The print is also known as Gaifū Kaisei

thunderstorm-beneath-summit.title: Thunderstorm Beneath the Summit
thunderstorm-beneath-summit.description: Mount Fuji darkened and struck by lightning, from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
descriptions: Hokusai created this print around 1831 in the Mount Fuji series
Lightning streaks the dark base of the volcano at the distant foot
The work plays on the contrast between the calm summit and the storm below
The print is preserved in several international collections
Hokusai signed this series Iitsu, his artist name at the time

sudden-shower-ohashi.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake
sudden-shower-ohashi.description: Pouring rain on the bridge, a print that inspired Van Gogh.
descriptions: Hiroshige created this print in 1857 in the Hundred Views of Edo
The rain is depicted by fine lines engraved in series
Van Gogh copied this print in oil in 1887
The work is preserved at the Brooklyn Museum in New York
The Ōhashi Bridge spanned the Sumida river in Edo (Tokyo)

plum-garden-kameido.title: Plum Garden at Kameido
plum-garden-kameido.description: Plum branches in the foreground, copied by Van Gogh.
descriptions: Hiroshige created this print in 1857 in the Hundred Views of Edo
Van Gogh copied this work in oil in 1887 in Paris
The foreground branch distorts traditional perspective
The work is preserved at the Brooklyn Museum in New York
The Kameido garden was famous for the shogun's plum trees

shono-driving-rain.title: Driving Rain at Shōno
shono-driving-rain.description: Travelers in pouring rain, from the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.
descriptions: Hiroshige created this print in 1833 in the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō
Shōno was the 46th station of the road connecting Edo to Kyoto
The work is among Hiroshige's most famous prints
The print exists in many editions from the Edo period
Whistler and the Impressionists admired these bold compositions

eagle-susaki.title: Eagle Flying over the Susaki Pine Forest
eagle-susaki.description: Eagle in soaring flight above a snowy landscape, from the One Hundred Views of Edo.
descriptions: Hiroshige created this print in 1857 in the Hundred Views of Edo
Susaki was a coastal district of Edo near Tokyo Bay
The eagle dives into a snowy, silent landscape
The work is preserved at the Brooklyn Museum in New York
Hiroshige died in 1858 shortly after completing the series
